nodes.title: Geometric local L-homomorphisms
nodes.statement: Let G be a connected reductive group over F and ϕ : W_F → LG(C) a continuous semisimple L-homomorphism (compatible with the projection to the Galois factor). For a finite-dimensional algebraic representation τ : LG → GL_N write ρ(ϕ, τ) = τ ∘ ϕ. The parameter ϕ is geometric when, for a faithful τ, every eigenvalue λ of ρ(ϕ, τ)(Frob) is a Weil q-number of integer weight: λ is algebraic over Q and there is w(λ) ∈ ℤ with |σ(λ)| = q^{w(λ)/2} for every field embedding σ : Q(λ) → ℂ. The weight multiset of ϕ along τ is the multiset of the w(λ), counted with algebraic multiplicity. The same definition applies with C = Q̄_ℓ, and to a Weil-group representation W_F → GL_N(C) (the case LG = GL_N).
hypotheses: F = k((t)) is a local field of characteristic p with residue field k of cardinality q, W_F its Weil group and Frob ∈ W_F a geometric Frobenius lift (it acts on k̄ by x ↦ x^{1/q}); C is an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 (C = ℂ or C = Q̄_ℓ).

Frobenius conventions are those of the parent roadmap: geometric Frobenius, local reciprocity sending a uniformizer to geometric Frobenius, and one fixed square root of q for normalized induction and half Tate twists.

The Weil parameter is Frobenius-semisimple and has finite inertia image. Finite inertia is an admissibility hypothesis here; an ℓ-adic representation with quasi-unipotent inertia is first converted to its Weil–Deligne representation. A semisimple algebraic representation alone is not used as a substitute for this hypothesis.
proofSteps: The eigenvalues of τ(ϕ(Frob)) are those of an endomorphism of a finite-dimensional space, so the Weil-number predicate of DWP.0 applies to each of them.
Independence of the chosen faithful τ and of the Frobenius lift is the theorem RA.0/geometricity-is-intrinsic; the definition fixes one faithful τ and one lift.
acceptance: For G = G_m over F₄((t)) and ϕ unramified with ϕ(Frob) = 2, ϕ is geometric of weight 1; with ϕ(Frob) = 3 it is not, since |3| is not an integer power of 4^{1/2}.
A parameter whose Frobenius eigenvalues all have complex absolute value 1 under the given inclusion but are transcendental is not geometric.

nodes.title: Geometricity is independent of the realization
nodes.statement: Let ϕ : W_F → LG(C) be a continuous semisimple L-homomorphism. (a) If the eigenvalues of τ₀(ϕ(Frob)) are Weil q-numbers of integer weights for one faithful τ₀, then for every algebraic representation τ of LG the eigenvalues of τ(ϕ(Frob)) are Weil q-numbers of integer weights. (b) The condition does not depend on the Frobenius lift: for Frob′ = Frob·σ with σ in inertia, the eigenvalues of τ(ϕ(Frob′)) are Weil q-numbers of the same weights. (c) For an algebraic L-homomorphism f : LG → LH, geometricity of ϕ implies that of f ∘ ϕ, with equivalence when f is a closed embedding.
hypotheses: F = k((t)) is a local field of characteristic p with residue field k of cardinality q, W_F its Weil group and Frob ∈ W_F a geometric Frobenius lift (it acts on k̄ by x ↦ x^{1/q}); C is an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 (C = ℂ or C = Q̄_ℓ).
τ₀ is faithful: its kernel is trivial as a group scheme.
The parameter has finite inertia image, as in RA.0/geometric-l-homomorphism.
proofSteps: (a) A faithful representation of an affine algebraic group is a tensor generator: every algebraic τ is a subquotient of a finite sum of τ₀^{⊗a} ⊗ (τ₀^∨)^{⊗b} (Deligne–Milne Proposition 2.20(b), the tensor-generator statement imported through RD.6).

Eigenvalues of tensor products and duals are products and inverses of eigenvalues (DWP.0/spectra-of-tensor-products-and-duals), and eigenvalues of a subquotient are among those of the ambient endomorphism; Weil q-numbers of integer weight are closed under products and inverses (DWP.0/weil-number-arithmetic).

(b) By the finite-inertia hypothesis ϕ(I_F) is finite, say of order m, normalized by ϕ(Frob). Some power ϕ(Frob)^N with N ≥ 1 commutes with ϕ(I_F); then ϕ(Frob′)^{Nm} = ϕ(Frob)^{Nm}, so the eigenvalues of τ(ϕ(Frob′)) are Nm-th roots of those of τ(ϕ(Frob))^{Nm}. A root of a Weil q^{Nm}-number of weight w is a Weil q-number of weight w (DWP.0/weil-number-base-extension).
(c) τ ∘ f is an algebraic representation of LG, so (a) applies; for a closed embedding f a faithful representation of LH restricts to a faithful one of LG.
acceptance: For G = SL₂ (Ĝ = PGL₂) and ϕ unramified with ϕ(Frob) = diag(q^{1/2}, q^{−1/2}) (the trivial representation), the adjoint representation has eigenvalues q, 1, q^{−1} with weights 2, 0, −2.
If the condition held only for a non-faithful τ (say the trivial representation) nothing would follow; faithfulness is needed.

nodes.title: Pure Weil–Deligne representations and parameters
nodes.statement: A Weil–Deligne representation (ϕ, N) of W_F on a finite-dimensional C-vector space V (ϕ continuous and Frobenius-semisimple, N nilpotent with ϕ(w) N ϕ(w)^{−1} = q^{−deg w} N for w ∈ W_F, deg(Frob) = 1) is pure of weight w ∈ ℤ when: (i) the eigenvalues of ϕ(Frob) are Weil q-numbers of integer weights; (ii) for each a the sum W_a V of the generalized eigenspaces of ϕ(Frob) of weight ≤ a is stable under ϕ and N (N lowers weights by 2); (iii) for every i ≥ 0, N^i induces an isomorphism gr_{w+i} V → gr_{w−i} V, where gr_a = W_a/W_{a−1}. For a fixed field isomorphism ι : C ≅ ℂ, ι-purity of weight w uses the same integer filtration and N-isomorphisms, replacing the Weil-number condition by 2 log_q|ι(λ)| ∈ ℤ. Arithmetic purity requires the same weights for every embedding as well as algebraicity of the eigenvalues. For semisimple G, call an LG-valued pair arithmetically pure of weight 0 when τ ∘ (ϕ,N) is arithmetically pure of weight 0 for every algebraic τ. For general reductive G use the separate analytic predicate ι-essentially tempered: the associated W_F × SL₂ parameter has bounded Weil image after projection to the adjoint group. No common-weight condition in one arbitrary faithful representation is used for reductive groups. The associated semisimple parameter is ϕ(w) = φ(w,diag(q^{−deg w/2},q^{deg w/2})), with N = dφ(e); thus N lowers weights by 2.
hypotheses: F = k((t)) is a local field of characteristic p with residue field k of cardinality q, W_F its Weil group and Frob ∈ W_F a geometric Frobenius lift (it acts on k̄ by x ↦ x^{1/q}); C is an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 (C = ℂ or C = Q̄_ℓ).

Frobenius conventions are those of the parent roadmap: geometric Frobenius, local reciprocity sending a uniformizer to geometric Frobenius, and one fixed square root of q for normalized induction and half Tate twists.
This is the geometric-Frobenius form of Ciubotaru–Harris Definition 2.6 with the correction PAPER-CIUBOTARU-HARRIS-26/E9: as printed, (ii) and (iii) ask N to move weights in opposite directions.
The Weil part has finite inertia image. A direct summand below is a Weil–Deligne direct summand, respecting both ϕ and N.
proofSteps: The Weil–Deligne relation with geometric Frobenius gives ϕ(Frob)(Nv) = q^{−1} N ϕ(Frob)v, so N maps the generalized λ-eigenspace to the q^{−1}λ one and lowers weights by 2; this makes (ii) consistent with (iii).

Tensor products of pure WD representations have added weights and duals have opposite weights. WD direct summands inherit purity of the same weight. Arbitrary subobjects and quotients need not: in Sp(2), ker N has weight 0 while the whole pair is pure of weight 1 (Taylor–Yoshida Lemma 1.4(5), pp. 6–7). The all-representations group predicate avoids assuming the false common-weight faithful criterion.

For the Frobenius-semisimple dictionary use the WD–SL₂ equivalence with the displayed sign convention. Jacobson–Morozov supplies the algebraic SL₂; the arithmetic purity conditions and analytic boundedness are compared only after fixing ι, as specified in RA.0/pure-completion-uniqueness.
acceptance: The special representation Sp(2): V = C², ϕ(Frob) = diag(1, q) on (e₀, e₁), N e₁ = e₀, N e₀ = 0, is pure of weight 1: gr₀ = ⟨e₀⟩, gr₂ = ⟨e₁⟩ and N : gr₂ → gr₀ is an isomorphism.
The same ϕ with N = 0 is not pure of any weight.

nodes.title: Uniqueness of pure completions
nodes.statement: For a fixed ι, a GL_n WD representation is ι-pure of weight 0 iff the Weil part of its associated L-parameter is bounded. For a general reductive group, a Frobenius-semisimple Weil parameter has at most one ι-essentially tempered WD completion up to Ĝ-conjugacy; essential temperedness means adjoint boundedness. In particular an arithmetic weight-0 completion of a semisimple-group parameter, if it exists, is unique. Arithmetic purity is not equivalent to boundedness at just one embedding.
hypotheses: F = k((t)) is a local field of characteristic p with residue field k of cardinality q, W_F its Weil group and Frob ∈ W_F a geometric Frobenius lift (it acts on k̄ by x ↦ x^{1/q}); C is an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 (C = ℂ or C = Q̄_ℓ).
C = ℂ for boundedness; for C = Q̄_ℓ transport by a field isomorphism Q̄_ℓ ≅ ℂ (ι-purity).
proofSteps: For GL_n decompose the WD representation into special representations Sp(r); ι-purity of weight 0 says that the primitive Weil constituents have exactly the shifts cancelling the SL₂ weights, hence the associated Weil part is bounded. Taylor–Yoshida Lemma 1.4(3) compares its arithmetic version with temperedness at every embedding; it does not remove that quantifier.

For uniqueness use Gan–Harris–Sawin Lemma 3.5(b): after projection to the adjoint group the Weil part is bounded; its centralizer is reductive, and its SL₂ lies in the derived subgroup of the identity component. The neutral element is determined by the real Frobenius part of the given semisimple parameter.

Apply neutral-element conjugacy to that semisimple derived Lie algebra (N0/neutral-conjugacy and N0/kostant-conjugacy). Lift back through the finite central isogeny; a connected SL₂ has no nontrivial morphism into the central torus. Unbounded central Weil characters do not affect this uniqueness argument.
acceptance: For GL₂ and ρ unramified with ρ(Frob) = diag(q^{1/2}, q^{−1/2}) (weights 1 and −1), the pure completion is the Steinberg parameter with N ≠ 0; N = 0 is not pure.
For GL₂, diag(1,q²) has no essentially tempered completion: with N=0 its two real Weil exponents differ, while the WD relation prevents a nonzero N from joining eigenvalues whose ratio is q².

Distinguishes arithmetic purity from temperedness at every embedding; direct summands of a pure WD representation inherit its weight, while arbitrary WD subobjects need the determinant condition.

nodes.title: Constant-field twist decomposition of a lisse sheaf
nodes.statement: Let V be a smooth curve over a finite field k₁ and L a lisse Q̄_ℓ-sheaf on V. Call two continuous characters χ, χ′ : Gal(k̄₁/k₁) → Q̄_ℓ^× equivalent when χ′χ^{−1}(Frob) is a Weil q₁-number of some integer weight. Then L decomposes uniquely as L = ⊕_{[χ]} L_χ ⊗ χ, the sum over representatives of the equivalence classes, where each L_χ is mixed with integer weights in the absolute sense (every Frobenius eigenvalue at every closed point is a Weil number of integer weight, with no choice of ι) and almost all L_χ vanish. The summand of the trivial class is the largest subsheaf with integer weights; L has integer weights iff L = L_1. For each ι : Q̄_ℓ ≅ ℂ this refines Deligne's decomposition by ι-weights modulo ℤ.
hypotheses: K = k₁(X) is the function field of a smooth projective geometrically connected curve X over a finite field k₁ of characteristic p and cardinality q₁; |X| is its set of closed points (places); q_w = |k(w)| for a place w; ℓ ≠ p is a prime.
V is smooth over k₁ (a dense open of a curve), L is lisse, χ is pulled back from Spec k₁.
proofSteps: Each irreducible constituent P of L is χ_P ⊗ P₀ with det P₀ of finite order (Deligne, Weil II Proposition 1.3.4; DWP.5/rank-one-normalization).

By L. Lafforgue (Théorème VII.6 and Proposition VII.7; GS.6/companions-on-curves) the Frobenius eigenvalues of P₀ are algebraic with all complex conjugates of absolute value 1, i.e. P₀ is pure of weight 0 in the absolute sense.

Group the constituents by the class of χ_P; on the summand attached to a class choose one representative χ and write χ_P = χ·(χ_Pχ^{−1}) with χ_Pχ^{−1} pure of integer weight; this gives L_χ mixed with integer weights.

Use L. Lafforgue Corollaire VII.8 directly for the absolute constant-twist decomposition, including the splitting of extensions between distinct twist classes. DWP.8 supplies the analogous fixed-ι decomposition; disjoint spectra by itself proves no-Hom, not the required Ext vanishing.
acceptance: On V = Spec k₁ with q₁ = 4 the rank-one sheaf with Frobenius 3 is χ ⊗ 1 for a class [χ] ≠ [1].
If L has integer weights everywhere then L = L_1.

nodes.title: One geometric boundary place makes a local system geometric
nodes.statement: Let L be a lisse Q̄_ℓ-sheaf on V = X ∖ |S| and u ∈ S a missing place with local Weil representation ρ_u of W_{K_u} on the generic geometric fibre. If ρ_u^{ss} is geometric (RA.0/geometric-l-homomorphism with G = GL_n), then: (a) for every w ∉ S the Frobenius eigenvalues of ρ_w(Frob_w) are Weil q_w-numbers of integer weights; (b) L has a unique increasing filtration W_• by lisse subsheaves with gr_i = W_i/W_{i−1} punctually pure of weight i, and dim gr_i equals the number n(i) of Frobenius eigenvalues of weight i at any w ∉ S, independently of w; (c) the Weil–Deligne representation of W_{K_u} on (gr_i L) at u is pure of weight i (RA.0/pure-weil-deligne-parameter).
hypotheses: K = k₁(X) is the function field of a smooth projective geometrically connected curve X over a finite field k₁ of characteristic p and cardinality q₁; |X| is its set of closed points (places); q_w = |k(w)| for a place w; ℓ ≠ p is a prime.
S is a nonempty finite set of places and L is lisse on X ∖ |S|; the same conclusions hold when u is a place where L is unramified and ρ_u(Frob_u) has Weil-number eigenvalues.
proofSteps: Decompose L = ⊕ L_χ ⊗ χ by RA.1/constant-field-weight-decomposition; each L_χ ⊗ χ is a sum of pieces χ′ ⊗ P with P pure of weight 0 for every ι and χ′ in the class of χ.

Deligne's local weight–monodromy theorem (DWP.5/local-monodromy-purity) for P at u: the monodromy graded pieces have Frobenius eigenvalues of ι-weight i for every ι, with i read off from the monodromy filtration, which does not depend on ι; hence these eigenvalues are Weil numbers (DWP.0/weil-number-iff-iota-pure-for-every-iota).

Geometricity of ρ_u^{ss} forces χ′(Frob_u) = χ′(Frob)^{deg u} to be a Weil number of integer weight, so every class is trivial; L has integer weights and (a) follows at w ∉ S (DWP.0/weil-number-base-extension).
(b) is Deligne's punctual weight filtration for a lisse mixed sheaf with integer weights (DWP.8/punctual-weight-filtration-3-4-1-ii); the count n(i) is constant in w because gr_i is pure of weight i.

(c) gr_i L is lisse and punctually pure of weight i, so DWP.5/local-monodromy-purity gives monodromy graded pieces of weight i + j at u, which is purity of weight i in the sense of RA.0 (after the E9 correction).
acceptance: For the Kloosterman sheaf Kl_n on G_m over F_q (pure of weight n − 1, tame at 0 with unipotent monodromy), the place u = 0 is geometric and W_• has the single nonzero graded piece gr_{n−1} = Kl_n.
The rank-one sheaf with Frobenius 3 on G_{m,F₄} is not geometric at any place, and the conclusion fails.

sources.match: States that geometricity of the local monodromy at one boundary place makes every unramified fibre geometric, that L has a filtration with pure graded pieces whose ranks count the eigenvalues of each weight, and that the graded pieces are pure Weil–Deligne representations at the boundary place; it attributes the result to Deligne's Weil II.
Supplies the decomposition by constant-field twist classes on which the propagation argument rests.

nodes.title: Purity of irreducible Ĝ-valued local systems
nodes.statement: Let Ĝ be semisimple over Q̄_ℓ and σ : Gal(K^sep/K) → Ĝ(Q̄_ℓ) continuous, unramified outside a finite set, such that V ∘ σ is ι-mixed for one faithful V (automatic on curves by RA.1/constant-field-weight-decomposition). If the image of σ lies in no proper parabolic subgroup of Ĝ, then V ∘ σ is ι-pure of weight 0 for every representation V of Ĝ. For LG-valued σ with Ĝ semisimple the same argument applies when parabolic subgroups of LG are taken in the dynamic sense (GHS Lemma 3.6 and Remark 3.7 note that the argument holds for any reductive G, giving a common weight for each irreducible algebraic representation; semisimplicity of Ĝ forces the weight to be 0 as in the last step below).
hypotheses: K = k₁(X) is the function field of a smooth projective geometrically connected curve X over a finite field k₁ of characteristic p and cardinality q₁; |X| is its set of closed points (places); q_w = |k(w)| for a place w; ℓ ≠ p is a prime.
ι : Q̄_ℓ ≅ ℂ is fixed; the conclusion is then for every ι, since the hypothesis is ι-independent.

Fixed-ι mixedness permits real weights. Apply the decomposition modulo ℤ followed by a constant twist before using DWP.8 integer-indexed weight filtrations; alternatively use the real-weight version of the argument in Sawin–Templier §11.
proofSteps: Use the real-weight filtration on an ι-mixed sheaf, as in Sawin–Templier §11, Lemma 11.4, p.83. DWP.8 gives its integer-weight case; after splitting by weights modulo ℤ and applying constant twists it supplies the required filtration on the separate summands. The Frobenius cocharacter construction below is the real-weight version and must use the full faithful representation, not a single irreducible summand.

At an unramified place v let T be a torus containing the semisimple part of Frob_v; the linear function ω(χ) = log|ι(χ(Frob_v^{ss}))| on characters of T is increasing along the filtration, and the stabilizer is the subgroup generated by T and the root subgroups on which ω is ≥ 0.
That subgroup is parabolic unless ω vanishes on all roots; as Ĝ is semisimple, ω then vanishes on all characters of T, so V ∘ σ is pure of weight 0.
acceptance: For Ĝ = SL₂ and σ = χ ⊕ χ^{−1} with χ(Frob) of weight 1 the image lies in a Borel subgroup and the weights are ±1: the irreducibility hypothesis is necessary.
For Ĝ = SL₂ and σ the monodromy of the Legendre family twisted by q^{−1/2}, σ is irreducible and pure of weight 0.

sources.match: Proves that an ι-mixed representation into a semisimple dual group whose image lies in no proper parabolic subgroup is pure of weight zero after composition with every representation, by comparing the weight filtration with the parabolic attached to a Frobenius torus.
Uses this lemma with the dynamic definition of parabolic subgroups of LG and notes that the argument holds for any reductive G, the mixedness hypothesis being supplied by L. Lafforgue.

nodes.title: Local Weil–Deligne purity of irreducible global parameters
nodes.statement: Let G be semisimple over K and σ a continuous semisimple global Galois parameter whose image lies in no proper parabolic of LG. At every place u, the Frobenius-semisimple WD representation of τ ∘ σ|_{W_{K_u}} is arithmetically pure of weight 0 for every algebraic τ. Its LG-valued WD completion is therefore the unique essentially tempered completion at every ι. For a general reductive group the corresponding assertion is about the adjoint projection; a common arithmetic weight for every τ is not asserted.
hypotheses: K = k₁(X) is the function field of a smooth projective geometrically connected curve X over a finite field k₁ of characteristic p and cardinality q₁; |X| is its set of closed points (places); q_w = |k(w)| for a place w; ℓ ≠ p is a prime.

G is a connected semisimple group over K; Ĝ is its dual group over the coefficient field and LG = Ĝ ⋊ Gal(K̃/K), with K̃/K the finite Galois extension through which Gal(K^sep/K) acts on the based root datum (Galois form, as in GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands GS.5).
proofSteps: By RA.1/sawin-templier-purity, τ ∘ σ is pure of some weight (weight 0 for semisimple G) for every τ.

Deligne's local monodromy theorem (DWP.5/local-monodromy-purity) gives that the i-th monodromy graded piece at z is pure of weight w + i; so the Frobenius eigenvalues are Weil numbers and the weight filtration is the monodromy filtration, which is condition (iii) of purity.
Uniqueness is RA.0/pure-completion-uniqueness.
acceptance: For G = PGL₂ and σ attached to a cuspidal π with π_z Steinberg, the local parameter at z is Sp(2) twisted to weight 0, pure with N ≠ 0.

sources.locator: §3.2, Lemma 3.6 with its proof and Corollary 3.8, pp. 9–10; Remark 3.13, p. 11
sources.match: Deduces from Sawin–Templier and Deligne's Theorem 1.8.4 that the restriction of an irreducible global parameter to any decomposition group is a pure Weil–Deligne parameter, and that it is the unique pure completion of the local semisimple parameter of a local component of a cuspidal representation with irreducible parameter; the purity is of some weight, ι-pure for every ι (Remark 3.13), and weight 0 for semisimple G comes from the Sawin–Templier argument.

nodes.title: Cuspidal representations belonging to a parameter
nodes.statement: Let A₀(G, U, E) be the module of E-valued cusp forms of level U (FA.6) and A₀(G, U, Q̄_ℓ) = ⊕_σ A₀(G, U, Q̄_ℓ)_{λ(σ)} V. Lafforgue's decomposition into generalized eigenspaces of the excursion algebra B(G, U, Q̄_ℓ), indexed by continuous semisimple σ : Gal(K^sep/K) → LG(Q̄_ℓ) unramified outside S (GS.5); Φ(U) is the set of σ that occur. For an irreducible π ⊂ A₀(G, Q̄) with m_U(π) ≠ 0, π belongs to σ ∈ Φ(U) when the restriction λ_H(σ) of λ(σ) to the spherical Hecke algebra H^S(G, U) away from S equals the action of H^S(G, U) on π^U (after ι_ℓ). For an algebraic representation τ : LG → GL_M, L(σ, τ) is the semisimple lisse Q̄_ℓ-sheaf on X ∖ |S| given by τ ∘ σ, and L(π, τ) := L(σ, τ) when π belongs to σ.
hypotheses: K = k₁(X) is the function field of a smooth projective geometrically connected curve X over a finite field k₁ of characteristic p and cardinality q₁; |X| is its set of closed points (places); q_w = |k(w)| for a place w; ℓ ≠ p is a prime.

Q̄ is the algebraic closure of Q inside C, and ι : Q̄ → C, ι_ℓ : Q̄ → Q̄_ℓ are fixed embeddings; a statement 'for every ι' quantifies over all field embeddings Q̄ → C, equivalently over all field isomorphisms Q̄_ℓ ≅ C after extension.

G is a connected semisimple group over K; Ĝ is its dual group over the coefficient field and LG = Ĝ ⋊ Gal(K̃/K), with K̃/K the finite Galois extension through which Gal(K^sep/K) acts on the based root datum (Galois form, as in GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands GS.5).
U ⊂ G(A_K) is a compact open subgroup and S = S(U) is the finite set of places w at which U_w = U ∩ G(K_w) is not a hyperspecial maximal compact subgroup; at w ∉ S the group G is unramified over K_w.
proofSteps: The decomposition and the parameters σ are GS.5/the-main-decomposition (split G) and GS.5/nonsplit-groups-and-the-l-group (general G); the excursion algebra contains the spherical Hecke operators away from S (GS.5/the-excursion-algebra, Ciubotaru–Harris Lemma 3.5).
τ ↦ L(σ, τ) is a symmetric monoidal functor from Rep(LG) to semisimple lisse sheaves on X ∖ |S| (GHS Corollary 2.4(i)).
acceptance: For τ trivial, L(π, τ) is the constant sheaf Q̄_ℓ.
Belonging is a relation, not a function: when two parameters have the same Satake classes away from S, π may belong to both (Ciubotaru–Harris §9.1 notes the same issue when m(π) > 1).

sources.locator: §3.1, decomposition (3.3), Lemma 3.5 and Definition 3.7, pp. 9–10; §5, equation (5.3), p. 13
sources.match: Recalls Lafforgue's decomposition of cusp forms over the excursion algebra, the compatibility of its Hecke part with the rational Hecke action, defines when a cuspidal representation belongs to a parameter and attaches the local systems L(π, τ).

States Lafforgue's map to semisimple global parameters with Satake compatibility, and that composing with representations of LG gives a symmetric monoidal functor to completely reducible local systems.

nodes.title: Rationality of Lafforgue's Satake classes
nodes.statement: For σ ∈ Φ(U) and w ∉ S let s_{w,ℓ}(σ) ∈ [LG_ss(Q̄_ℓ)] be the Satake class of λ_w(σ). Then s_{w,ℓ}(σ) = ι_ℓ(s_w(σ)) for a class s_w(σ) ∈ [LG_ss(Q̄)], and s_{w,ℓ}(σ) = [σ(Frob_w)]. Consequently the eigenvalues of τ(σ(Frob_w)) are algebraic numbers for every τ, and if π belongs to σ then ι(s_v(σ)) is the Satake parameter of the unitary spherical representation π_v ⊗_ι ℂ for every v ∉ S.
hypotheses: K = k₁(X) is the function field of a smooth projective geometrically connected curve X over a finite field k₁ of characteristic p and cardinality q₁; |X| is its set of closed points (places); q_w = |k(w)| for a place w; ℓ ≠ p is a prime.

Q̄ is the algebraic closure of Q inside C, and ι : Q̄ → C, ι_ℓ : Q̄ → Q̄_ℓ are fixed embeddings; a statement 'for every ι' quantifies over all field embeddings Q̄ → C, equivalently over all field isomorphisms Q̄_ℓ ≅ C after extension.

G is a connected semisimple group over K; Ĝ is its dual group over the coefficient field and LG = Ĝ ⋊ Gal(K̃/K), with K̃/K the finite Galois extension through which Gal(K^sep/K) acts on the based root datum (Galois form, as in GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands GS.5).
U ⊂ G(A_K) is a compact open subgroup and S = S(U) is the finite set of places w at which U_w = U ∩ G(K_w) is not a hyperspecial maximal compact subgroup; at w ∉ S the group G is unramified over K_w.
proofSteps: A₀(G, U, E) is a finite E-module with A₀(G, U, E) ⊗ C ≅ A₀(G, U, C) for noetherian Z[1/p]-algebras E ⊂ C (FA.6/integral-coefficient-model, Ciubotaru–Harris Proposition 3.1 after BHKT Proposition 8.2); for a large number field E the action of H^S(G, U) ⊗ E is semisimple with finitely many eigencharacters, which take algebraic values (Lemma 3.2).
The Hecke part of the excursion action is the Q̄_ℓ-linear extension of the rational Hecke action (GS.3/hecke-operator-as-creation-frobenius-annihilation; Lafforgue Proposition 6.2).

Lafforgue's Theorem 11.11 (GS.5/the-main-decomposition, GS.5/satake-compatibility-and-chebotarev) identifies the Satake class of λ_w(σ) with [σ(Frob_w)] through the normalized Satake isomorphism (FA.6/function-field-hecke-satake, SR.4/satake-isomorphism).
Cusp forms are compactly supported modulo the centre (FA.6/harder-cuspidal-support), so the Petersson inner product makes π ⊗_ι ℂ unitary; its spherical components are unitary.
acceptance: For G = PGL₂ the class s_w(σ) is diag(α_w, α_w^{−1}) with α_w + α_w^{−1} = q_w^{−1/2} a_w, a_w the T_w-eigenvalue: algebraic, as a_w is.

sources.match: Proves algebraicity of cuspidal Hecke eigenvalues from the finiteness of integral cusp forms, recalls that the Hecke part of the excursion algebra is the rational Hecke action, deduces that Lafforgue's Satake classes are images of algebraic classes equal to the Frobenius classes of the parameter, and notes that the place-v class is the Satake parameter of a unitary spherical representation.

nodes.title: The real part of a Satake class
nodes.statement: For σ ∈ Φ(U), w ∉ S and an embedding ι, write ι(s_w(σ)) = s_c·q_w^{ν} with s_c in the maximal compact subgroup of T̂(ℂ) and ν ∈ t̂_ℝ (polar decomposition, SRU.5/real-satake-parameter). The real part is ν_w^ι(σ) := ν = log_{q_w}|ι(s_w(σ))| ∈ t̂_ℝ, well defined up to the (relative) Weyl group. Its pairing with a weight α of τ gives half the Deligne ι-weight of the corresponding eigenvalue of τ(σ(Frob_w)): |ι(·)| = q_w^{⟨α, ν⟩}. Thus that Deligne weight is 2⟨α,ν⟩.
hypotheses: K = k₁(X) is the function field of a smooth projective geometrically connected curve X over a finite field k₁ of characteristic p and cardinality q₁; |X| is its set of closed points (places); q_w = |k(w)| for a place w; ℓ ≠ p is a prime.

Q̄ is the algebraic closure of Q inside C, and ι : Q̄ → C, ι_ℓ : Q̄ → Q̄_ℓ are fixed embeddings; a statement 'for every ι' quantifies over all field embeddings Q̄ → C, equivalently over all field isomorphisms Q̄_ℓ ≅ C after extension.

G is a connected semisimple group over K; Ĝ is its dual group over the coefficient field and LG = Ĝ ⋊ Gal(K̃/K), with K̃/K the finite Galois extension through which Gal(K^sep/K) acts on the based root datum (Galois form, as in GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands GS.5).
U ⊂ G(A_K) is a compact open subgroup and S = S(U) is the finite set of places w at which U_w = U ∩ G(K_w) is not a hyperspecial maximal compact subgroup; at w ∉ S the group G is unramified over K_w.
For nonsplit G at w the real part lies in the τ-fixed part (t̂_ℝ)^τ (SRU.6/tau-fixed-dual-group).
proofSteps: The polar decomposition of T̂(ℂ) = T̂_ℝ·T̂_c is unique; Weyl-conjugate classes give Weyl-conjugate real parts.
For a weight α of τ the eigenvalue α(ι s_w) has absolute value q_w^{⟨α, ν⟩} because α(s_c) has absolute value 1.
acceptance: For G = PGL₂ and the trivial representation at w, ν = ½α̂ (pairing ±½ with the weights of the standard representation of SL₂).
For the complementary-series parameter diag(q^{1/4}, q^{−1/4}) of PGL₂, ν pairs to ¼ with a weight of the standard representation.

sources.match: Defines the real part of the Satake parameter at an unramified place as the logarithm to base q of its absolute value under a complex embedding, and records that a spherical representation is tempered exactly when this real part vanishes.
Writes every Satake parameter uniquely as a compact part times a real part.

nodes.title: Uniformization of global shtukas by local shtukas
nodes.statement: Let C be the curve of a global function field, v a place with formal disc D, G connected reductive with a smooth model, legs I placed in D with bounds μ_•, and N a level disjoint from v. Gluing a framed local G-shtuka to the trivial G-bundle away from v by Beauville–Laszlo defines a formally étale morphism Θ̂ from the formal moduli of local G-shtukas bounded by μ_• to the formal completion along v of the moduli of global G-shtukas of level N (Li-Huerta Proposition 5.13). On a Harder–Narasimhan truncation ≤ s and for deg N large enough this is a morphism of formal schemes, formally étale and locally formally of finite type (Proposition 5.14). On generic fibres, for every n ≥ 0, it gives an étale morphism Θ_n of locally spatial diamonds from the analytic local shtuka moduli with level n·v to the diamond of the truncated global moduli with level n·v + N (Theorem 5.16), compatible with the partial Frobenius morphisms (Lemma 5.18). Through Θ_n the homology of the local shtuka moduli with Satake coefficients maps to the cohomology of the global shtuka stacks (§6).
hypotheses: K = k₁(X) is the function field of a smooth projective geometrically connected curve X over a finite field k₁ of characteristic p and cardinality q₁; |X| is its set of closed points (places); q_w = |k(w)| for a place w; ℓ ≠ p is a prime.
N and v are disjoint; deg N is large enough for Proposition 5.14; the truncation ≤ s is fixed and Θ_n is defined over the product of the punctured discs at v.
proofSteps: A framed local shtuka includes the quasi-isogeny trivialization on the punctured disc. Glue its bundles and modifications to the trivial bundle and identity modifications away from v; the level N is trivial there. This defines Θ̂ in the local-to-global direction. Rigidity of quasi-isogenies (Proposition 2.3) gives the unique infinitesimal lifting required by Proposition 5.13.
On truncations the source is a formal scheme by Li-Huerta Theorem 2.12 and the target by the finite-type statement for large deg N (Proposition 5.14).

Pass to generic fibres through the analytic local shtuka moduli and their identification with diamonds (Theorem 4.9, Proposition 4.12) to define Θ_n with level at v (Theorem 5.16); compatibility with partial Frobenius is Lemma 5.18.
The coefficient sheaves on both sides match under Θ_n (Lemma 6.4), which gives the maps on (co)homology used in §6.13.
acceptance: For G=GL₁, use a local shtuka with its quasi-isogeny framing. Gluing produces a global line bundle trivialized away from v, of degree prescribed by the local modification. Forgetting the framing does not define the stated local-to-global map, and formal étaleness does not assert a bijection with all global Pic-shtuka components.

sources.match: Constructs the uniformization morphism from local to global shtuka moduli: formally étale on formal stacks, a formally étale morphism of formal schemes on Harder–Narasimhan truncations for large tame level, and an étale morphism of locally spatial diamonds on generic fibres with level at v, compatible with partial Frobenius.

sources.locator: §§2–4, Theorem 2.12, Theorem 4.9 and Proposition 4.12, pp. 8–33; §6, Lemma 6.4 and §6.13, pp. 42–47
sources.match: Builds the formal and analytic moduli of local shtukas in equal characteristic used as the source of the morphism, and compares local and global coefficient sheaves to map local homology to global cohomology.

nodes.title: Li-Huerta: Lafforgue's global parameters are locally Fargues–Scholze
nodes.statement: Let G be connected reductive over a global function field K, v a place and Π a cuspidal automorphic representation. Then the semisimplification of the restriction to W_{K_v} of Lafforgue's global parameter of Π equals the Fargues–Scholze semisimple parameter of Π_v. Consequently the Genestier–Lafforgue semisimple local parametrization of irreducible smooth representations of G(F), F of characteristic p, agrees with the Fargues–Scholze parametrization; at the level of Bernstein centres the excursion elements of the two constructions coincide.
hypotheses: K = k₁(X) is the function field of a smooth projective geometrically connected curve X over a finite field k₁ of characteristic p and cardinality q₁; |X| is its set of closed points (places); q_w = |k(w)| for a place w; ℓ ≠ p is a prime.
Coefficients Q̄_ℓ with ℓ ≠ p; the mod-ℓ analogue also holds (Li-Huerta Theorem 6.15).
proofSteps: Through the uniformization morphism (RA.3/shtuka-uniformization) the local excursion algebra acting on the homology of local shtuka moduli maps to the global excursion algebra (Li-Huerta Theorem 6.13).
Comparing the Fargues–Scholze Bernstein-centre elements (ES5) with Lafforgue's global excursions (GS.5/excursions-on-full-compact-cohomology) gives Theorem 6.15 and then Theorem A (§6.16).

Genestier–Lafforgue's parameters satisfy the same local–global compatibility (GS.7/local-global-compatibility-up-to-semisimplification) and globalization of every irreducible representation's Bernstein-centre character forces agreement (Theorem C, §7.2).
acceptance: At an unramified place both parameters are the Satake parameter, so the theorem is known there before the proof (Li-Huerta remark after Theorem A).

nodes.title: Properties of the semisimple local parametrization
nodes.statement: Let L_F : Π(G/F) → Φ(G/F) be the semisimple local parametrization of irreducible smooth Q̄_ℓ-representations (Genestier–Lafforgue, equal to Fargues–Scholze by RA.3/li-huerta-compatibility). Then: (1) for F = K_w and Π cuspidal, L_F(Π_w) = (L(Π)|_{W_F})^{ss}; (2) if π is a constituent of the normalized induction i_P^G(ρ), then L_F(π) = i_M ∘ L_F(ρ) for the Levi embedding i_M : LM → LG; (3) if L_F(π) lies in no proper Levi subgroup, π is supercuspidal; (4) if π has nonzero vectors under the pro-p radical of an Iwahori subgroup of a quasi-split G, L_F(π) factors through LT; (5) for Υ : G₁ → G₂ with normal image, L_F(π ∘ Υ) = LΥ ∘ L_F(π) on constituents; (6) τ ↦ τ ∘ L_F(π) is symmetric monoidal; (7) coefficient transport by γ fixing the chosen √q commutes with L_F; for a general γ the precise finite central normalization twist is a requested ES5 target (G8), rather than an unverified formula through a named cocharacter.
hypotheses: F = k((t)) is a local field of characteristic p with residue field k of cardinality q, W_F its Weil group and Frob ∈ W_F a geometric Frobenius lift (it acts on k̄ by x ↦ x^{1/q}); C is an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 (C = ℂ or C = Q̄_ℓ).

Frobenius conventions are those of the parent roadmap: geometric Frobenius, local reciprocity sending a uniformizer to geometric Frobenius, and one fixed square root of q for normalized induction and half Tate twists.
G connected reductive over F.
proofSteps: (1) is GS.7/local-global-compatibility-up-to-semisimplification (Genestier–Lafforgue Théorème 0.1).

(2) and (3): compatibility with normalized parabolic induction (GS.7/bernstein-center-and-local-parameters; ES7:parabolic/normalised-induction-dictionary); if π were a constituent of an induction from a proper parabolic, its parameter would factor through a proper Levi.

(4) follows from (2) for a principal-series constituent. (5) uses the general normal-image functoriality of GHS Theorem 2.3(vi), requested explicitly at ES6; the existing isogenies node alone has the narrower adjoint-isomorphism hypothesis.

(7) is the coefficient-transport target requested at ES5, including the precise effect of moving √q on the normalized parameter. The existing invariance-and-coefficient-transport supplier is conditional and does not by itself identify this twist. No characteristic-zero GL_n comparison is used here.
acceptance: For GL₂ the Steinberg representation and the trivial representation have the same semisimple parameter diag(q^{1/2},q^{−1/2}), by their common normalized-induction support. This is an equal-characteristic calculation and does not cite ES7’s characteristic-zero GL_n comparison.
For the Steinberg representation of PGL₂, L_F(St) is unramified with Frobenius diag(q^{1/2}, q^{−1/2}): the parameter of the trivial representation, as (2) predicts.

sources.match: Recalls the semisimple local parametrization with local–global compatibility, compatibility with parabolic induction and the supercuspidality of representations with irreducible parameter.

nodes.title: Geometric representations of a local group
nodes.statement: An irreducible smooth representation π of G(F) over Q̄_ℓ is geometric when it has a model π_E over a number field E ⊂ Q̄_ℓ (π_E ⊗_E Q̄_ℓ ≅ π) and its semisimple parameter L_F(π) is geometric (RA.0/geometric-l-homomorphism). A complex representation is geometric when it is π ⊗_{ι} ℂ for a geometric π.
hypotheses: F = k((t)) is a local field of characteristic p with residue field k of cardinality q, W_F its Weil group and Frob ∈ W_F a geometric Frobenius lift (it acts on k̄ by x ↦ x^{1/q}); C is an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 (C = ℂ or C = Q̄_ℓ).
G connected reductive over F; L_F as in RA.3/local-parametrization.
proofSteps: The definition is stable under the choice of the faithful representation and of Frobenius (RA.0/geometricity-is-intrinsic).
The number-field model is part of the datum: it is what makes Galois conjugates π_E ⊗_{E,ι′} Q̄_ℓ meaningful.
acceptance: The trivial representation of any G is geometric: its parameter has Frobenius q^{ρ̂}, with eigenvalues integral powers of q^{1/2}.
An unramified character of G_m(F) with value 3 on a uniformizer, q = 4, is not geometric.

nodes.title: Galois conjugates of geometric representations
nodes.statement: If π is geometric with model π_E, then π_E ⊗_{E, ι′} Q̄_ℓ is geometric for every embedding ι′ : E → Q̄_ℓ.
hypotheses: F = k((t)) is a local field of characteristic p with residue field k of cardinality q, W_F its Weil group and Frob ∈ W_F a geometric Frobenius lift (it acts on k̄ by x ↦ x^{1/q}); C is an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 (C = ℂ or C = Q̄_ℓ).
G connected reductive over F.
Use the coefficient-transport contract requested at ES5, including the finite central normalization twist for automorphisms moving √q (G8).
proofSteps: Extend the two embeddings of the number field to an automorphism γ of Q̄_ℓ. The requested ES5 coefficient-transport contract identifies L_F(γπ) with γL_F(π), allowing the specified finite central normalization twist. The representation twist is an autoequivalence preserving irreducibility and smoothness by the current SR.0 coefficient-change target; a transported number-field model is still a number-field model.
Being a Weil q-number of a given integer weight depends only on the minimal polynomial (DWP.0/weil-q-number), so γ preserves it; −1 is a Weil number of weight 0.
acceptance: For an unramified character of G_m with value (1 + 2i) on a uniformizer and q = 5, the conjugate value (1 − 2i) again has absolute value √5.

sources.match: States that conjugates of a geometric representation by embeddings of its field of definition are geometric, deducing it from compatibility of the Genestier–Lafforgue and Fargues–Scholze parametrizations with automorphisms of the coefficient field.

nodes.title: Geometric characters of tori
nodes.statement: For a split F-torus T, a smooth character χ : T(F) → Q̄_ℓ^× is geometric iff all its values are Weil q_F-numbers of integer weight. For T = Res_{E/F} G_m, let f=[k_E:k_F] and q_E=q_F^f. Then χ is geometric iff χ(ϖ_E) is a Weil q_E-number of integer weight; the values on O_E^× are roots of unity. The criterion must use q_E, not q_F. For an arbitrary nonsplit torus retain the definition through its torus L-parameter; the all-values condition with q_F is not asserted to be sufficient.
hypotheses: F = k((t)) is a local field of characteristic p with residue field k of cardinality q, W_F its Weil group and Frob ∈ W_F a geometric Frobenius lift (it acts on k̄ by x ↦ x^{1/q}); C is an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 (C = ℂ or C = Q̄_ℓ).
T a torus over F (not necessarily split).
proofSteps: For G_m use local reciprocity, sending ϖ_F to geometric Frobenius. Smoothness makes the image of the compact unit group finite; a split torus is a finite product of this calculation. Algebraicity of the finitely many uniformizer values also supplies a number-field model.

For Res_{E/F} G_m use the induced L-representation Ind_{W_E}^{W_F} χ. For unramified E/F its Frobenius eigenvalues λ satisfy λ^f=χ(ϖ_E), up to root-of-unity factors. Thus 2 log_{q_F}|λ| = 2 log_{q_E}|χ(ϖ_E)|, with the same equality for every conjugate. For ramified E/F, the same power argument uses the residue degree f and finite inertia.

An isogeny or a resolution by induced tori does not remove this residue-degree constraint. For unramified quadratic E/F and χ(ϖ_E)=q_F^{1/2}, every character value is a Weil q_F-number of integer weight, but the induced Frobenius eigenvalues ±q_F^{1/4} have weight 1/2, so χ is not geometric.
acceptance: For the unramified quadratic torus Res_{E/F} G_m, χ(ϖ_E)=q_F has weight 1 relative to q_E and gives induced Frobenius weights 1; χ(ϖ_E)=q_F^{1/2} fails integrality.
For split G_m the values on units have weight 0 and the sole unramified weight is 2 log_{q_F}|χ(ϖ_F)|, independent of the embedding precisely for a Weil number.

sources.match: Proposition 3.10(2) states the all-values criterion for a general torus; this is used only for split tori here. Weil restriction requires q_E=q_F^f and gives the counterexample in this packet E2.

nodes.title: Stability of geometricity
nodes.statement: Geometricity of irreducible smooth representations is preserved by: constituents of normalized parabolic induction i_P^G(ρ) from geometric ρ; constituents of the normalized Jacquet module r_P(π) of geometric π; external tensor products for G₁ × G₂; and twisting by geometric characters of G(F) factoring through G → G^{ab}.
hypotheses: F = k((t)) is a local field of characteristic p with residue field k of cardinality q, W_F its Weil group and Frob ∈ W_F a geometric Frobenius lift (it acts on k̄ by x ↦ x^{1/q}); C is an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 (C = ℂ or C = Q̄_ℓ).
G connected reductive over F, P = MN a parabolic subgroup.
proofSteps: Induction: L_F(π)=i_M∘L_F(ρ). The normalized induced object is defined over a number field after adjoining √q. For induction and Jacquet modules use finite length and admissibility, choose a compact open subgroup whose invariants see all constituents, and use the finite-dimensional image of its Hecke algebra over that number field. Its simple modules descend after finite coefficient extension; the simple Hecke-module/smooth-representation correspondence then gives number-field models of the constituents. Coefficient change of invariants and of the functors is already in SR.0/SR.2; it does not alone assert descent of arbitrary infinite-length objects.

For a Jacquet constituent η on M, its cuspidal support, viewed in G, is G-conjugate to the cuspidal support of π, by the geometric lemma and the cuspidal-support theorem. Compatibility with normalized induction therefore identifies i_M∘L_M(η) with L_G(π). Since i_M is a closed embedding, RA.0/geometricity-is-intrinsic(c) gives geometricity of L_M(η).
Products and twists: ES6:functoriality/products and ES6:functoriality/twisting-by-abelianized-characters, with RA.3/geometric-torus-characters for the character.
acceptance: Every irreducible constituent of an unramified principal series of PGL₂ induced from a character with value q^{1/2} on a uniformizer is geometric (the trivial and Steinberg representations).

sources.match: States that geometricity is preserved under normalized parabolic induction, Jacquet modules, direct products and twists by geometric characters.

nodes.title: Central characters of geometric representations
nodes.statement: Let π be geometric. For every F-split torus A contained in Z_G, the restricted central character ω_π|_{A(F)} is geometric and hence takes Weil q_F-number values of integer weight. More generally, the restriction to T=(Z_G)_red^∘ is geometric through the torus local parameter, provided the normal-image central functoriality requested at ES6 is supplied. No L-group of a nonsmooth centre is formed. For example the centre μ_p of SL_p in characteristic p is not a torus; its group of F-points is trivial.
hypotheses: F = k((t)) is a local field of characteristic p with residue field k of cardinality q, W_F its Weil group and Frob ∈ W_F a geometric Frobenius lift (it acts on k̄ by x ↦ x^{1/q}); C is an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 (C = ℂ or C = Q̄_ℓ).
G connected reductive over F with centre Z_G.
proofSteps: For a smooth central torus T→G the image is normal, so the normal-image compatibility of GHS Theorem 2.3(vi) identifies the parameter of ω_π|_T with the composite LT←LG←W_F. This precise extension of the ES6 central-character supplier is requested; the existing z-embedding supplier alone does not make a nonsmooth centre a torus.

Composition with an algebraic L-map preserves geometricity by RA.0/geometricity-is-intrinsic. In the split case RA.3/geometric-torus-characters converts this into the values criterion. This is exactly the input on the split centres A_M required in Casselman inequalities.
acceptance: For G = GL_n and π = St_n, ω_π is trivial.

sources.match: States that the central character of a geometric representation of any reductive group is geometric, because restriction to the centre corresponds to representations of LG factoring through the L-group of the centre.

nodes.title: ι-tempered and ι-discrete representations
nodes.statement: Let π be an irreducible admissible representation of G(F) defined over Q̄ and ι : Q̄ → ℂ an embedding. π is ι-tempered (resp. ι-discrete series) when π ⊗_{Q̄, ι} ℂ is tempered (resp. square-integrable modulo the centre) in the sense of SR.3. π is tempered (resp. discrete series) in the absolute sense when this holds for every embedding ι′.
hypotheses: F = k((t)) is a local field of characteristic p with residue field k of cardinality q, W_F its Weil group and Frob ∈ W_F a geometric Frobenius lift (it acts on k̄ by x ↦ x^{1/q}); C is an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 (C = ℂ or C = Q̄_ℓ).
G connected reductive over F; π irreducible admissible over Q̄.
proofSteps: Temperedness of π ⊗_ι ℂ requires a unitary central character together with Casselman’s inequalities on the exponents of proper normalized Jacquet modules (SR.3/casselman-criterion). Coefficient change transports these algebraic characters and exponent values by ι′.
Hence ι-temperedness depends only on the absolute values |ι(χ(a))| of the exponents χ of π.
acceptance: If all exponents of π are Weil q-numbers of integer weights, ι-temperedness does not depend on ι.
The definition requires a Q̄-model; a complex representation without such a model has no ι-conjugates.

sources.locator: §4.1, Definition 4.1 and the paragraph after it, p. 11
sources.match: Defines ι-temperedness of a representation with algebraic coefficients through its complex base change along ι, temperedness as ι′-temperedness for all embeddings, and notes that a unitary central character for one embedding need not stay unitary for another.

nodes.title: Globalizing supercuspidals with irreducible parameter
nodes.statement: Let G be connected semisimple over a global function field K, z a place with K_z ≅ F and π a supercuspidal representation of G(F). There are infinitely many cuspidal automorphic Π of G(A_K) with Π_z ≅ π whose global parameter L(Π) lies in no proper parabolic subgroup of LG. Hence L_F(π) has a pure completion realized as the restriction of L(Π) to the decomposition group at z.
hypotheses: K = k₁(X) is the function field of a smooth projective geometrically connected curve X over a finite field k₁ of characteristic p and cardinality q₁; |X| is its set of closed points (places); q_w = |k(w)| for a place w; ℓ ≠ p is a prime.
G connected semisimple over K; z a place of K.

In this packet the Galois-parameter and arithmetic-purity conclusion is planned for semisimple G. The general reductive extension requires central-character normalization and compatible global central data, recorded in G8.
proofSteps: Choose a place x ≠ z where G is split (infinitely many: places splitting completely in a splitting field).

At x take the local component π′ at ∞ of the Heinloth–Ngô–Yun Kloosterman automorphic representation over P¹_{k(x)}; its parameter is the Kloosterman Ĝ-local system (KB.1/eigenobject, identified with Lafforgue's parameter by Satake compatibility and Chebotarev, GHS Remark 3.10), whose inertia image at ∞ has no adjoint invariants (KB.6/rigidity-local; Xu–Zhu remove the HNY prime restrictions, KB.11/all-prime-corollaries), so L_F(π′) lies in no proper Levi. The KB.6 supplier currently states isocrystal local invariants; the étale HNY vanishing and its Xu–Zhu all-prime transfer are an explicit requested extension, not an implicit change of cohomology theory.
Gan–Lomelí's Poincaré-series globalization gives cuspidal Π with Π_x ≅ π′, Π_z ≅ π and tame components elsewhere (requested from FA.6).
L(Π)|_{W_x}^{ss} = L_F(π′) (RA.3/local-parametrization (1)) is irreducible, so L(Π) is; RA.1/local-purity-of-irreducible-parameters gives the pure completion at z.

Use the vanishing of adjoint inertia invariants to exclude a proper Levi: a proper Levi of a semisimple dual group has a positive-dimensional centre, whose Lie algebra would be fixed. This is weaker than irreducibility of the adjoint Weil representation, and the latter is not used (this packet E4).
acceptance: For G = PGL₂ the Kloosterman parameter at ∞ is the Kloosterman sheaf Kl₂, whose ∞-inertia acts irreducibly (Swan conductor 1).

sources.locator: §3.3, Proposition 3.9 and its proof, Remark 3.10, pp. 10–11
sources.match: Constructs, for a supercuspidal at one place, infinitely many cuspidal globalizations with irreducible global parameter, using the Kloosterman representation at an auxiliary split place (with Xu–Zhu removing the prime restrictions of Heinloth–Ngô–Yun) and the Poincaré-series globalization of Gan–Lomelí.

Globalizes prescribed supercuspidals at a finite set of places to a cuspidal representation whose other local components are depth-zero principal series constituents, with prescribed central character.
Computes, for split almost-simple G, that the adjoint Kloosterman local system has Swan conductor equal to the rank at ∞ and no inertia invariants there, for p good when G is not simply laced.

nodes.title: Beuzart-Plessis's pseudo-globalization of discrete series
nodes.statement: Let G be connected reductive over K with Z⁰ the identity component of its centre, ξ a character of Z⁰(K)∖Z⁰(A_K), S_ram the places where G or ξ ramify, and S, S′ ⊂ |X| disjoint with S′ ∩ S_ram = ∅. For v ∈ S let π_v be discrete series with central character ξ_v on Z⁰(K_v), at least one π_{v₀} supercuspidal; for v ∈ S′ let X_v be a proper Zariski-closed subset of the unramified characters with central character ξ_v. Then there is a cuspidal automorphic Π with central character ξ on Z⁰(A_K) such that Π_v has nonzero trace against a pseudo-coefficient of π_v for v ∈ S (so Π_v and π_v have the same cuspidal support), and Π_v is unramified with Satake parameter outside X_v for v ∈ S′. It is not asserted that Π_v ≅ π_v for v ∈ S ∖ {v₀}.
hypotheses: K = k₁(X) is the function field of a smooth projective geometrically connected curve X over a finite field k₁ of characteristic p and cardinality q₁; |X| is its set of closed points (places); q_w = |k(w)| for a place w; ℓ ≠ p is a prime.
G connected reductive over K; pseudo-coefficients exist by the trace Paley–Wiener theorem.

S and S′ are finite. The central torus formulation assumes Z_G^∘ is smooth; for a nonsmooth centre use its maximal smooth connected central torus and supply the corresponding central-character formulation.
proofSteps: Choose f = ⊗f_v: pseudo-coefficients at S (a matrix coefficient of π_{v₀}^∨ at v₀), Hecke functions at S′ whose Satake transforms vanish on X_v, units almost everywhere, and support meeting only regular elliptic classes.
Apply the Deligne–Kazhdan simple trace formula: the spectral side counts exactly the Π of the conclusion.

Find a regular elliptic δ ∈ G(K) with nonzero local orbital integrals at S ∪ S′ (Lemma A.3), using weak approximation up to the finite-index open closure of G(K) in G(K_{S∪S′}) and Beuzart-Plessis's elliptic orthogonality for discrete-series characters; shrink an auxiliary support so that only δ contributes.
acceptance: For S = {v₀} (one supercuspidal) the conclusion gives Π_{v₀} ≅ π_{v₀}: a matrix coefficient of a supercuspidal detects it.

sources.locator: Appendix A (R. Beuzart-Plessis), Lemma A.1 and its proof with Lemma A.3, pp. 38–40
sources.match: Proves the existence of a cuspidal representation with nonzero traces against pseudo-coefficients of prescribed discrete series at a finite set of places (one of them supercuspidal) and unramified components avoiding prescribed closed sets elsewhere, via the Deligne–Kazhdan simple trace formula.

sources.locator: §8, Lemma 8.1 and Proposition 8.2 with the remark after it, pp. 38–40
sources.match: Shows that nonzero trace against a pseudo-coefficient gives the same supercuspidal support; proves the semisimple-group version of the globalization conditionally on its Working Hypothesis II (a simple trace formula), which Beuzart-Plessis's lemma replaces; and states explicitly that the global representation need not have the prescribed discrete series as local component.

nodes.title: Discrete series parameters realized in irreducible global parameters
nodes.statement: For semisimple G and an essentially discrete series π of G(F), there is a cuspidal automorphic Π of G over a global function field K with K_z ≅ F such that L_F(Π_z) = L_F(π) and L(Π) lies in no proper parabolic subgroup. Hence L_F(π) admits a pure completion L(π), realized as the restriction of L(Π) at z.
hypotheses: K = k₁(X) is the function field of a smooth projective geometrically connected curve X over a finite field k₁ of characteristic p and cardinality q₁; |X| is its set of closed points (places); q_w = |k(w)| for a place w; ℓ ≠ p is a prime.
G connected semisimple; any K, z with K_z ≅ F and G defined over K (as in GHS).

In this packet the Galois-parameter and arithmetic-purity conclusion is planned for semisimple G. The general reductive extension requires central-character normalization and compatible global central data, recorded in G8.
proofSteps: Take x and π′ as in RA.4/supercuspidal-irreducible-globalization.

Apply RA.4/discrete-series-pseudo-globalization with S = {x, z}, π_x = π′ supercuspidal and π_z = π: Π_x ≅ π′ and Π_z has the cuspidal support of π, so L_F(Π_z) = L_F(π) by RA.3/local-parametrization (2).
L(Π) is irreducible since its restriction at x is; RA.1/local-purity-of-irreducible-parameters.
acceptance: For PGL₂ the only infinite-dimensional constituent with the cuspidal support of St is St itself, so Π_z ≅ St (local components of cuspidal representations of PGL₂ are generic); for groups with non-generic cuspidal representations, such as Sp₄, Π_z may be a non-tempered constituent with the same support, and only the common semisimple parameter is used.

sources.match: Proves that an essentially discrete series representation has the same semisimple parameter as a local component of a cuspidal representation with irreducible global parameter, using the appendix lemma, and stresses that the local component need not be the given discrete series.

nodes.title: Weil–Deligne purity of discrete series
nodes.statement: For connected reductive G and a discrete-series π, the semisimple local parameter has a unique essentially tempered WD refinement at a fixed ι (GHS Theorem 1.2). The refinement is essentially tempered after every coefficient embedding in the adjoint sense. For semisimple G, every algebraic τ of LG gives an arithmetically pure WD representation of weight 0, so its semisimple Frobenius eigenvalues have integer weights symmetric about 0. For general reductive G no single arithmetic weight in an arbitrary faithful representation is asserted; the proof requires the central reduction in G8.
hypotheses: F = k((t)) is a local field of characteristic p with residue field k of cardinality q, W_F its Weil group and Frob ∈ W_F a geometric Frobenius lift (it acts on k̄ by x ↦ x^{1/q}); C is an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 (C = ℂ or C = Q̄_ℓ).
G connected reductive over F of any characteristic p (the published version has no restriction on p; the arXiv v3 version assumed p > 3).
proofSteps: For semisimple G, existence follows from RA.4/discrete-series-irreducible-globalization and RA.1/local-purity-of-irreducible-parameters; uniqueness is RA.0/pure-completion-uniqueness. For reductive G, first twist the central character by an unramified character to reduce its unramified part to finite order, and compare discrete series and parameters under central isogenies/z-extensions. These exact local reduction and parameter-transport statements are requested at SR.3/ES6 (G8); they cannot be replaced by the semisimple globalizations alone.
The semisimple global input is pure for every embedding. The reductive assertion concerns adjoint boundedness, which is unchanged by central twists (GHS Remark 3.13 read with this convention).

For semisimple G use Sawin–Templier for each ι and every algebraic τ, plus the absolute weight argument through constant-twist classes; the determinant of τ factors through a finite Galois quotient, forcing the common weight to be 0. GHS Corollary 3.12 states the adjoint case, and the same semisimple argument applies to any τ.

For semisimple G, arithmetic purity of every τ ∘ L_F(π) gives integer-weight Weil-number Frobenius eigenvalues. This yields geometricity when the representation also has the number-field model required in RA.3/geometric-representation. No such central arithmetic assertion follows for general reductive G from adjoint boundedness alone.
acceptance: For G = PGL₂ and π = St, L(π) is the Steinberg parameter and τ = standard of SL₂ gives Sp(2) twisted by q^{−1/2}: weights 1 and −1, pure of weight 0.

nodes.title: Discrete series with algebraic models are geometric
nodes.statement: Let G be semisimple over F and π a representation with a number-field model such that π ⊗_ι ℂ is discrete series. Then π is geometric. The extension to general reductive G with a geometric central character is a remaining target in G8, requiring the precise central reduction and torus convention; it is not inferred merely by taking a root of a nonzero integer-weight Weil number.
hypotheses: F = k((t)) is a local field of characteristic p with residue field k of cardinality q, W_F its Weil group and Frob ∈ W_F a geometric Frobenius lift (it acts on k̄ by x ↦ x^{1/q}); C is an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 (C = ℂ or C = Q̄_ℓ).
proofSteps: Choose a field isomorphism Q̄_ℓ ≅ ℂ restricting to ι ∘ ι_ℓ^{−1} on ι_ℓ(Q̄); then π ⊗ Q̄_ℓ is a discrete series for that isomorphism and RA.4/weil-deligne-purity-of-discrete-series applies.
Purity of τ ∘ L(π) gives Weil-number Frobenius eigenvalues of integer weight.
acceptance: The Steinberg representation of PGL₂(F) is geometric with weights ±1 in the standard representation.

nodes.title: Galois conjugates of discrete series are discrete series
nodes.statement: Let G be semisimple over F and π an irreducible representation with a number-field model, viewed over Q̄ such that π ⊗_ι ℂ is discrete series for one ι. Then π ⊗_{ι′} ℂ is discrete series for every ι′ : Q̄ → ℂ. The assertion of Ciubotaru–Harris Theorem 4.2 that every complex discrete series of G(F) has a number-field model is not established by the cited argument (gap G2).
hypotheses: F = k((t)) is a local field of characteristic p with residue field k of cardinality q, W_F its Weil group and Frob ∈ W_F a geometric Frobenius lift (it acts on k̄ by x ↦ x^{1/q}); C is an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 (C = ℂ or C = Q̄_ℓ).

π is assumed to have a number-field model, viewed over Q̄; this holds for local components of cuspidal representations (RA.2/rational-satake-parameters) and for supercuspidals (RA.4/supercuspidal-irreducible-globalization). Descent for an arbitrary complex discrete series remains G2.
proofSteps: By RA.4/geometric-discrete-series, L_F(π) is geometric; the exponents of π (central characters of the constituents of its Jacquet modules on the split centres A_M) are geometric by RA.3/geometricity-stability and RA.3/geometric-central-characters, so their values are Weil q-numbers of integer weights.
Casselman's strict inequalities for ι (SR.3/casselman-criterion) are inequalities between integer weights, which do not depend on the embedding; hence π ⊗_{ι′} ℂ is square-integrable.
acceptance: For PGL₂ the Steinberg representation and the supercuspidals have conjugates of the same kind for every ι.

sources.match: States that complex discrete series have number-field models whose Galois conjugates are discrete series, attributing it to Gan–Harris–Sawin, and sketches a proof via globalization, geometricity of the exponents and Casselman's criterion; the globalization step only gives the same cuspidal support (source issue GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglandsPartII/E1).

nodes.title: Embedding independence of temperedness for geometric components
nodes.statement: Let Π be a cuspidal automorphic representation of semisimple G over K, defined over a number field, and v a place such that L_F(Π_v) is geometric. If Π_v is ι-tempered for one ι then it is tempered (for every ι′). Without the geometricity hypothesis the statement (Ciubotaru–Harris Theorem 4.3) is not established (PAPER-CIUBOTARU-HARRIS-26/E10; gap G3).
hypotheses: K = k₁(X) is the function field of a smooth projective geometrically connected curve X over a finite field k₁ of characteristic p and cardinality q₁; |X| is its set of closed points (places); q_w = |k(w)| for a place w; ℓ ≠ p is a prime.

G is a connected semisimple group over K; Ĝ is its dual group over the coefficient field and LG = Ĝ ⋊ Gal(K̃/K), with K̃/K the finite Galois extension through which Gal(K^sep/K) acts on the based root datum (Galois form, as in GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands GS.5).
proofSteps: Every irreducible constituent of every normalized Jacquet module of Π_v is geometric by RA.3/geometricity-stability. Its central character restricted to the split centre A_M therefore has Weil-number values by RA.3/geometric-central-characters. The central character of Π_v is unitary (Π is cuspidal semisimple); apply Casselman to these actual Jacquet exponents rather than identifying them with the supercuspidal support.
Casselman's criterion (SR.3/casselman-criterion) is then an inequality between integer weights, independent of ι.
acceptance: When L_F(Π_v) is unramified with Satake parameter of real part 0 for one ι and Weil-number eigenvalues, temperedness holds for all ι.

sources.locator: §4.1, Theorem 4.3 and step (2) of the sketch, p. 11
sources.match: Asserts that an ι-tempered local component of a cuspidal representation is tempered for every embedding; the sketch assumes that the local monodromy of every L(Π, τ) is geometric, which is the gap recorded as E10 by the extraction.

nodes.title: Test representations of the dual group
nodes.statement: For G absolutely simple over K, let G^{ad} be its adjoint group, whose dual Ĝ_sc is simply connected. The test set T(G) consists of the adjoint representation of Ĝ_sc and, by type of G: A_{n−1} with n even, the standard representation V(ω̂₁) of SL_n; B_n, the standard representation V(ω̂_n) of Sp_{2n}; C_n, the spin representation V(ω̂₁) of Spin_{2n+1}; D_n, the half-spin V(ω̂₁) and the vector representation V(ω̂_n) of Spin_{2n} (Ciubotaru–Harris numbering); E₇, the 56-dimensional V(ω̂₇); for A_{n−1} with n odd, E₆, E₈, F₄ and G₂, the adjoint representation alone. For G not adjoint these are representations of L(G^{ad}), used after lifting the parameter (RA.5/adjoint-lift). For the finite Galois L-group, replace each listed Ĝ_sc-module V by Ind_{Ĝ_sc}^{Ĝ_sc⋊Γ} V: its restriction is the direct sum of the Γ-translates of V. Thus the test list supplies algebraic L-group representations even when a fundamental highest weight is not Γ-fixed; the light Lean testWeights records only the underlying highest-weight indices.
hypotheses: G is a connected semisimple group over K; Ĝ is its dual group over the coefficient field and LG = Ĝ ⋊ Gal(K̃/K), with K̃/K the finite Galois extension through which Gal(K^sep/K) acts on the based root datum (Galois form, as in GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands GS.5).
G absolutely simple; numbering of fundamental weights as in Ciubotaru–Harris §6 and the SRU.5 nodes.
proofSteps: The list is the one for which SRU.5/fundamental-separators shows that every nonzero half-integral generic unitary point left by the adjoint representation is not half-integral for some member.

For a finite pinned action Γ, finite induction extends each module by taking ⊕_{γ∈Γ} {}^γV with Γ permuting the summands. The original module occurs as a direct summand after restriction, so integrality for the induced module implies integrality for the required separator. In type D the two half-spin translates must both be retained. Restriction to the folded group then uses SRU.6/nonsplit-generic-temperedness.
acceptance: For G = PGL₂ (n = 2) the test set is {adjoint, standard of SL₂}; for G = PGL₃ it is {adjoint}.

nodes.title: Lifting a parameter to the L-group of the adjoint group
nodes.statement: Let σ : Gal(K^sep/K) → LG(Q̄_ℓ) be continuous with image in LG(E) for a finite E/Q_ℓ, and LG^{ad} → LG the central extension dual to G → G^{ad} (kernel Z = ker(Ĝ_sc → Ĝ), a subgroup of the finite centre). There is a finite separable K′/K and a continuous lift σ̃′ : Gal(K^sep/K′) → LG^{ad}(Q̄_ℓ) of σ|_{Gal(K^sep/K′)}. For every place u′ of K′ over u, every τ ∈ T(G) and every place w′ unramified for σ̃′, the real part of σ̃′(Frob_{w′}) equals that of σ(Frob_{w′}), and τ ∘ σ̃′ is geometric at u′ when σ|_{u}^{ss} has a pure completion of weight 0. There is also a fixed-ι version: if the local completion has bounded Weil part at ι, every lifted algebraic representation has integer local ι-weights; this assertion does not imply arithmetic geometricity.
hypotheses: K = k₁(X) is the function field of a smooth projective geometrically connected curve X over a finite field k₁ of characteristic p and cardinality q₁; |X| is its set of closed points (places); q_w = |k(w)| for a place w; ℓ ≠ p is a prime.

G is a connected semisimple group over K; Ĝ is its dual group over the coefficient field and LG = Ĝ ⋊ Gal(K̃/K), with K̃/K the finite Galois extension through which Gal(K^sep/K) acts on the based root datum (Galois form, as in GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands GS.5).

This is needed when G is not adjoint and T(G) contains a representation not factoring through LG: types A_{n−1} (n even), B_n, C_n, D_n and E₇ (PAPER-CIUBOTARU-HARRIS-26/E12; the source writes the lift for types C and D only).
proofSteps: The image of σ is a compact ℓ-adic Lie group; an open subgroup lifts through the finite central extension (de Jong's remark, Ciubotaru–Harris footnote 6), giving K′; equivalently the obstruction in H²(Gal(K^sep/K), Z) dies on a finite extension.
At each fixed Frobenius the finite central kernel changes eigenvalues only by roots of unity. Compare real parts using the same residue field q_{w′}; the kernel is trivial if G is already adjoint.

The algebraic SL₂ of the local completion lifts through the central isogeny because SL₂ is simply connected. The real neutral element has integer eigenvalues in every representation, giving integer WD weights. A bounded Weil part lifts to a bounded Weil part; in the arithmetic case its eigenvalues are roots of Weil numbers of weight 0, which remain weight 0 at every embedding. This proves the distinct fixed-ι and arithmetic assertions.
acceptance: For G = SL₂ (Ĝ = PGL₂, LG^{ad} ∋ SL₂) a projective representation σ lifts to SL₂ after a finite extension killing its Brauer obstruction; the standard representation of SL₂ is then available.

sources.match: Reduces the non-adjoint case to the adjoint one by restricting the parameter to a finite extension over which it lifts to the L-group of the adjoint group, and composing the lift with τ₀; the footnote obtains the lift from an open subgroup of the compact image.

nodes.title: Integrality of Frobenius weights from a tempered place
nodes.statement: Let π ⊂ A₀(G, Q̄) belong to σ (RA.2/cuspidal-parameter-local-systems) and let u be a place. (a) If π_u is ι-tempered, then for every algebraic τ of LG the sheaf L(π, τ) has integer punctual ι-weights, and ⟨α, ν_w^ι(σ)⟩ ∈ ½ℤ for every weight α of τ and every w ∉ S. (b) If π_u is ι-discrete series, then for every τ the eigenvalues of τ(σ(Frob_w)), w ∉ S, are Weil q_w-numbers of integer weights (σ is geometric at every unramified place) and L(π, τ) has the weight filtration of RA.1/geometric-boundary-propagation. The same holds for τ ∈ T(G) composed with the lift σ̃′ of RA.5/adjoint-lift.
hypotheses: K = k₁(X) is the function field of a smooth projective geometrically connected curve X over a finite field k₁ of characteristic p and cardinality q₁; |X| is its set of closed points (places); q_w = |k(w)| for a place w; ℓ ≠ p is a prime.

Q̄ is the algebraic closure of Q inside C, and ι : Q̄ → C, ι_ℓ : Q̄ → Q̄_ℓ are fixed embeddings; a statement 'for every ι' quantifies over all field embeddings Q̄ → C, equivalently over all field isomorphisms Q̄_ℓ ≅ C after extension.

G is a connected semisimple group over K; Ĝ is its dual group over the coefficient field and LG = Ĝ ⋊ Gal(K̃/K), with K̃/K the finite Galois extension through which Gal(K^sep/K) acts on the based root datum (Galois form, as in GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands GS.5).
U ⊂ G(A_K) is a compact open subgroup and S = S(U) is the finite set of places w at which U_w = U ∩ G(K_w) is not a hyperspecial maximal compact subgroup; at w ∉ S the group G is unramified over K_w.
u may lie in S or outside it (PAPER-CIUBOTARU-HARRIS-26/E13).
proofSteps: (b) By RA.4/geometric-discrete-series π_u is geometric; by RA.3/local-parametrization (1) the semisimplified restriction of τ ∘ σ to W_{K_u} is τ ∘ L_F(π_u), hence geometric; apply RA.1/geometric-boundary-propagation to L(π, τ).

For (a), realize π_u inside normalized induction from a discrete series ρ of a Levi M with ι-unitary central character (SR.3). Use the reductive fixed-ι completion theorem RA.4/weil-deligne-purity-of-discrete-series, including its requested central reduction G8: the central real part is 0 and the SL₂ weights are integers. This gives local integer ι-weights without asserting arithmetic geometricity. Apply the mod-ℤ decomposition and local weight–monodromy theorem to eliminate every other weight class globally.
The half-integrality is RA.2/satake-real-part (halfIntegral_of_integerWeights).
For τ ∈ T(G) use RA.5/adjoint-lift at the places of K′.
acceptance: For PGL₂ a Steinberg anchor has normalized local weights ±1. The integrality conclusion by itself is not the Hasse bound for an elliptic curve; weight-0 automorphic normalization and purity require separate input.

sources.match: Uses the purity of the discrete-series parameter at u and the uniqueness of the twist decomposition (5.5) to show that every L(π, τ) is mixed with integer weights, so that the real part at every unramified place is half-integral (5.6); the tempered case reduces to the discrete series of a Levi subgroup.

nodes.title: The generic Ramanujan theorem over function fields
nodes.statement: Let G be connected absolutely simple over K and π ⊂ A₀(G, Q̄) with m_U(π) ≠ 0 belonging to σ. Assume (1) at a place v ∉ S where G_{K_v} is unramified quasi-split and not the quasi-split form of PSU(2n+1), π_v ⊗_ι ℂ is generic and the compact part of its Satake parameter ι(s_v(σ)) is equal to 1, or represented by z∈Z(Ĝ)^Γ giving a unitary unramified character twist. In the nonsplit case this condition concerns the dual-torus compact factor: the Frobenius component is kept separate and is not required to be central; (2) at a place u, π_u is ι-tempered. Then π_w ⊗_ι ℂ is tempered for every w ∉ S, and every irreducible constituent of every L(π, τ) is ι-pure of weight 0. If π_u is ι-discrete series, π_w is tempered for every embedding and every L(π, τ) is pure of weight 0.
hypotheses: K = k₁(X) is the function field of a smooth projective geometrically connected curve X over a finite field k₁ of characteristic p and cardinality q₁; |X| is its set of closed points (places); q_w = |k(w)| for a place w; ℓ ≠ p is a prime.

Q̄ is the algebraic closure of Q inside C, and ι : Q̄ → C, ι_ℓ : Q̄ → Q̄_ℓ are fixed embeddings; a statement 'for every ι' quantifies over all field embeddings Q̄ → C, equivalently over all field isomorphisms Q̄_ℓ ≅ C after extension.
U ⊂ G(A_K) is a compact open subgroup and S = S(U) is the finite set of places w at which U_w = U ∩ G(K_w) is not a hyperspecial maximal compact subgroup; at w ∉ S the group G is unramified over K_w.

G absolutely simple; v ∉ S so U_v is hyperspecial. The centrality condition at v is the scope correction of PAPER-CIUBOTARU-HARRIS-26/E11 (the source states the theorem without it); u may be any place (E13).
The source's abstract mentions a mild residue-field restriction coming from the arXiv version of Gan–Harris–Sawin; with the published version none is needed.
proofSteps: RA.5/integral-weights-from-anchor gives ⟨α, ν_v^ι(σ)⟩ ∈ ½ℤ for the adjoint representation and, through RA.5/adjoint-lift, for every τ ∈ T(G) (RA.5/test-representations).

π_v is unitary, spherical and generic. For adjoint G apply SRU.5 in the split case or SRU.6 in the nonsplit case, using their full-L-group central-compact hypotheses. For non-adjoint G use the central-isogeny transfer of spherical unitarity and genericity requested at SR.4/SRU.5: triviality on Z(G)(F) alone does not extend a representation from the image of G(F) to every element of G^ad(F). With this transfer and the lifted test modules the same local criterion gives ν_v^ι=0.

Then every constituent of L(π, τ) has ι-weight 0 at v; since the constituents are ι-pure of integer weight (previous step and DWP.8 weight filtration), they are all of weight 0, so ν_w^ι(σ) = 0 for every w ∉ S.

Temperedness at w: SRU.5/spherical-tempered-criterion (split) and Casselman's criterion (SR.3/casselman-criterion) in general. For the discrete-series anchor the weights are Weil numbers, so the conclusion holds for every ι.
acceptance: For G = PGL₂ and π_u Steinberg, the theorem is the Ramanujan conjecture for those π (known by Drinfeld); the hypothesis at v holds automatically, since every unramified generic unitary π_v of PGL₂ has Satake parameter with central compact part or is tempered.
The quasi-split PSU(2n+1) case is excluded: SRU.6/odd-unitary-residual leaves the point ½ω_n.
Without the centrality condition the local step fails: SRU.5/g2-noncentral-witness.

nodes.title: Propagation of genericity
nodes.statement: Under the hypotheses of RA.5/generic-ramanujan, π_w ⊗_ι ℂ is generic at every w ∉ S at which G_{K_w} is quasi-split; if G is quasi-split over K, π is locally generic at almost every place.
hypotheses: K = k₁(X) is the function field of a smooth projective geometrically connected curve X over a finite field k₁ of characteristic p and cardinality q₁; |X| is its set of closed points (places); q_w = |k(w)| for a place w; ℓ ≠ p is a prime.

Q̄ is the algebraic closure of Q inside C, and ι : Q̄ → C, ι_ℓ : Q̄ → Q̄_ℓ are fixed embeddings; a statement 'for every ι' quantifies over all field embeddings Q̄ → C, equivalently over all field isomorphisms Q̄_ℓ ≅ C after extension.

SRU.5 supplies the split adjoint special case; it does not alone prove the general nonsplit statement. The local theorem is the one invoked from Reeder Proposition 7.4 in Ciubotaru–Harris Corollary 5.7.
Apply this at every w ∉ S after RA.5/generic-ramanujan.

nodes.title: Elliptic global parameters
nodes.statement: For a continuous semisimple σ : Gal(K^sep/K) → LG(Q̄_ℓ) let S_σ be the centralizer in Ĝ of its image. σ is elliptic when S_σ / (Z(Ĝ))^{Gal(K̃/K)} is finite; equivalently (for semisimple σ) its image lies in no proper Levi subgroup of LG, equivalently (Ad⁰)^σ = 0 for the adjoint representation on Lie(Ĝ)/Lie(Z(Ĝ)).
hypotheses: K = k₁(X) is the function field of a smooth projective geometrically connected curve X over a finite field k₁ of characteristic p and cardinality q₁; |X| is its set of closed points (places); q_w = |k(w)| for a place w; ℓ ≠ p is a prime.

G is a connected reductive group over K; Ĝ is its dual group over the coefficient field and LG = Ĝ ⋊ Gal(K̃/K), with K̃/K the finite Galois extension through which Gal(K^sep/K) acts on the based root datum (Galois form, as in GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands GS.5).
proofSteps: Lie(S_σ) is the σ-invariant Lie algebra. Exactness of invariants for the finite Galois action in characteristic 0 identifies Lie(S_σ/(Z(Ĝ))^Γ) with (Lie(Ĝ)/Lie Z(Ĝ))^σ, so finiteness of the reductive quotient is equivalent to vanishing of these invariants.

A semisimple σ in a proper Levi M is centralized by the connected centre of M̂, a positive-dimensional torus modulo Z(Ĝ); conversely a positive-dimensional reductive S_σ contains a torus whose centralizer is a proper Levi containing the image.
acceptance: For G = GL_r, σ is elliptic iff it is irreducible (Lafforgue–Zhu §2); for G = PGL₂ (Ĝ = SL₂) every irreducible σ is elliptic and stable, its centralizer being ±1 by Schur's lemma.
For a torus every σ is elliptic.
