nodes.title: Elliptic parameters are tempered at unramified places
nodes.statement: Let G be semisimple over K, σ ∈ Φ(U) elliptic and π belonging to σ. Then L(σ, τ) is pure of weight 0 for every algebraic τ, and π_w ⊗_ι ℂ is tempered for every w ∉ S and every ι.
hypotheses: K = k₁(X) is the function field of a smooth projective geometrically connected curve X over a finite field k₁ of characteristic p and cardinality q₁; |X| is its set of closed points (places); q_w = |k(w)| for a place w; ℓ ≠ p is a prime.

Q̄ is the algebraic closure of Q inside C, and ι : Q̄ → C, ι_ℓ : Q̄ → Q̄_ℓ are fixed embeddings; a statement 'for every ι' quantifies over all field embeddings Q̄ → C, equivalently over all field isomorphisms Q̄_ℓ ≅ C after extension.

U ⊂ G(A_K) is a compact open subgroup and S = S(U) is the finite set of places w at which U_w = U ∩ G(K_w) is not a hyperspecial maximal compact subgroup; at w ∉ S the group G is unramified over K_w.
proofSteps: An elliptic semisimple σ lies in no proper parabolic (RA.6/elliptic-parameter), so RA.1/sawin-templier-purity gives purity of weight 0 for every τ and every ι.
Then ν_w^ι(σ) = 0 at every w ∉ S (RA.2/satake-real-part) and π_w is tempered (Sawin–Templier Lemma 11.5; SRU.5/spherical-tempered-criterion and SR.3/casselman-criterion).

The GL_r analogue additionally requires the finite-order central normalization and is not an example of the displayed semisimple hypothesis.

nodes.title: Lafforgue–Zhu decomposition over elliptic parameters
nodes.statement: Let G be split reductive over K, N a level, Ξ a cocompact central lattice and σ an elliptic parameter occurring in the cuspidal excursion decomposition. There is a finite-dimensional graded Q̄_ℓ-space A_σ with commuting actions of the full level-N Hecke algebra and 𝒮_σ=S_σ/Z(Ĝ), such that (H^cusp_{\{0\}∪I,W})_σ ≅ (A_σ⊗W_{σ^I})^{S_σ}, where W is an algebraic representation of Ĝ×(LG)^I, Γ^I acts through σ on the moving factors and trivially on the factor 0, and S_σ acts diagonally on all factors of W and through 𝒮_σ on A_σ. This is functorial in W, compatible with coalescence and level change. These generalized excursion eigenspaces are genuine eigenspaces and semisimple as Γ^I-representations; no Hecke semisimplicity of A_σ is asserted. With a suitable auxiliary representation at the frozen leg, each irreducible constituent of τ∘σ occurs in Satake-coefficient shtuka cohomology. The additional constant-coefficient realization of Expectation 5.9 requires the bridge G10.
hypotheses: K = k₁(X) is the function field of a smooth projective geometrically connected curve X over a finite field k₁ of characteristic p and cardinality q₁; |X| is its set of closed points (places); q_w = |k(w)| for a place w; ℓ ≠ p is a prime.

G split (the nonsplit case is conditional on extending Xue's finiteness to nonsplit groups, as Lafforgue–Zhu state); σ is one of Lafforgue's parameters, so it satisfies the conditions (C1)–(C5) of Lafforgue–Zhu §1 (finite coefficients, reductive Zariski closure, unramified outside a finite set, Galois projection, finite image in the abelianization).

The Satake-coefficient consequence uses a nonzero A_σ and a suitable auxiliary factor at the frozen leg. The constant-coefficient consequence suggested by Ciubotaru–Harris Remark 5.8 is conditional on G10.
proofSteps: Use Lafforgue–Zhu Proposition 1.2 and the extra frozen base leg: its Ĝ-representation W₀ supplies the central character needed for (A_σ⊗W₀⊗τ)^{S_σ} to contain the desired τ∘σ constituent. One must retain invariants under the full centralizer S_σ, including its connected centre; invariants under the finite quotient alone give a different formula. Lemma 4.1 supplies the nondeformability input to the proof, not a standalone assertion that every excursion algebra is reduced.
The cohomology functors are those of GS.3/the-functor-H-I-W with finiteness from GS.3/integral-cuspidal-finiteness.

The exact promotion from Satake-coefficient shtuka cohomology to constant-coefficient stack cohomology must be supplied: Satake IC sheaves are not constant sheaves. This realization bridge is recorded in G10; Proposition 1.2 by itself gives the displayed Satake-cohomology formula.
acceptance: For GL_r and irreducible σ, A_σ=π^{K_N} and (H^cusp_{I,W})_σ=π^{K_N}⊗(W^{G_m})_{σ^I} (Corollary 2.1, p.4). For a single moving standard factor without a compensating frozen factor, W^{G_m}=0, so the summand vanishes.

nodes.title: Realisability in the cohomology of stacks
nodes.statement: A semisimple lisse Q̄_ℓ-sheaf L on X ∖ |S| is realisable in stack cohomology when there are a finite set S′ ⊇ S, an algebraic stack Z of finite type over k₁ and a morphism f : Z → X ∖ |S′| such that every irreducible constituent of L|_{X∖|S′|} is a constituent of some Rⁱf_! Q̄_ℓ. Ciubotaru–Harris Expectation 5.9 asks this for L(π, τ) with τ adjoint and τ ∈ T(G); it is recorded here as a hypothesis, not a theorem.
hypotheses: K = k₁(X) is the function field of a smooth projective geometrically connected curve X over a finite field k₁ of characteristic p and cardinality q₁; |X| is its set of closed points (places); q_w = |k(w)| for a place w; ℓ ≠ p is a prime.
Algebraic stacks and Rf_! as in Laszlo–Olsson (stacky six operations).
proofSteps: Direct summands and restriction to a smaller open preserve the predicate. Tensor products use the fibre product of two witnessing stacks, Künneth and exactness on semisimplified finite-rank constituents. Verdier duality changes the constant coefficient sheaf to a dualizing complex and by itself does not prove closure of this constant-coefficient predicate under duals.
For elliptic σ, RA.6/lafforgue-zhu-decomposition gives the Satake-coefficient realization; the extra bridge to constant coefficients is an explicit hypothesis/request in G10.
acceptance: The constant sheaf is realisable with Z = X ∖ |S|.

nodes.title: Global Arthur homomorphism data
nodes.statement: Let C=Q̄_ℓ with its ℓ-adic topology. Global Arthur homomorphism data consist of a homomorphism ψ : W_K × SL₂(C) → LG(C), compatible with the projection to the Galois factor, continuous and unramified outside a finite set on W_K, Frobenius-semisimple at good places, and algebraic on SL₂, up to Ĝ(C)-conjugacy. Its nilpotent invariant is the class N_ψ of dψ(e) in Lie(Ĝ), e the upper unipotent generator of sl₂. At a place w where ψ is unramified, ψ_w : W_{K_w}/I_w × SL₂ → LG and j(Frob_w) = diag(q_w^{1/2}, q_w^{−1/2}); Ψ(G, U) is the set of classes unramified outside S(U). Here C=Q̄_ℓ has its ℓ-adic topology on the Weil part. Complex coefficient versions are obtained by field transport; no archimedean continuity of that transported global Weil map is asserted. Boundedness at good places is imposed separately in ArthurPrediction.At, not inferred from these weak homomorphism data.
hypotheses: K = k₁(X) is the function field of a smooth projective geometrically connected curve X over a finite field k₁ of characteristic p and cardinality q₁; |X| is its set of closed points (places); q_w = |k(w)| for a place w; ℓ ≠ p is a prime.

proofSteps: At an unramified place restrict the weak Weil homomorphism and evaluate it with the Arthur SL₂ as displayed. At a ramified place, converting the Weil representation to a WD representation introduces its monodromy/Deligne SL₂; merely restricting the weak homomorphism does not supply this additional factor.
N_ψ is defined by Jacobson–Morozov theory in Ĝ (LieHighestWeightPartII N0).
acceptance: Given weak data with trivial SL₂, N_ψ=0. They describe tempered local Satake classes only when the Weil restrictions at those places are bounded; triviality on SL₂ alone is insufficient.
For G = PGL₂ and ψ = 1 ⊠ (standard of SL₂ = Ĝ), ψ(Frob_w, j(Frob_w)) = diag(q_w^{1/2}, q_w^{−1/2}), the Satake parameter of the trivial representation.

nodes.title: Arthur's weight prediction at unramified places
nodes.statement: For a discrete automorphic π, global Arthur homomorphism data ψ and w ∉ S, π satisfies Arthur's prediction at w for ψ when: (a) the Satake class s(π_w) has integral weight (for every τ, τ(s(π_w)) is diagonalizable with eigenvalues Weil q_w-numbers of integer weight); (b) s(π_w) = ψ_w(Frob_w, j(Frob_w)) up to conjugacy; (c) ψ_w|_{W_{K_w}} is bounded after the chosen complex coefficient transport. π has place-independent weights when the multiset of weights of τ(s(π_w)) is the same for all w ∉ S and every τ, and determined by N_ψ (Expectation 1.9). When a single integer weight pattern determined by N_ψ is asserted arithmetically, impose (b) and (c) after every embedding. Boundedness at just one embedding need not give the same weights at its algebraic conjugates.

nodes.title: The parametrization hypotheses for the discrete spectrum
nodes.statement: The parametrization hypotheses for (G, U) are: (9.1) for every noetherian Z[1/p]-algebra E ⊂ C, A_disc(G, U, E) is a finite E-module and A_disc(G, U, E) ⊗ C ≅ A_disc(G, U, C); (9.5)(1) the excursion algebra acts on A_disc(G, U, Q̄_ℓ) and decomposes it as ⊕_σ A_disc(G, U, Q̄_ℓ)_{λ(σ)} (display (9.3)); (9.5)(2) for σ ∈ Φ_disc(U) and w ∉ S the Satake class of λ_w(σ) is ι_ℓ(s_w(σ)) with s_w(σ) ∈ [LG_ss(Q̄)] and equals [σ(Frob_w)]. A discrete π belongs to σ when π^U lies in the λ(σ)-summand.
hypotheses: K = k₁(X) is the function field of a smooth projective geometrically connected curve X over a finite field k₁ of characteristic p and cardinality q₁; |X| is its set of closed points (places); q_w = |k(w)| for a place w; ℓ ≠ p is a prime.

Q̄ is the algebraic closure of Q inside C, and ι : Q̄ → C, ι_ℓ : Q̄ → Q̄_ℓ are fixed embeddings; a statement 'for every ι' quantifies over all field embeddings Q̄ → C, equivalently over all field isomorphisms Q̄_ℓ ≅ C after extension.

G is a connected semisimple group over K; Ĝ is its dual group over the coefficient field and LG = Ĝ ⋊ Gal(K̃/K), with K̃/K the finite Galois extension through which Gal(K^sep/K) acts on the based root datum (Galois form, as in GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands GS.5).
U ⊂ G(A_K) is a compact open subgroup and S = S(U) is the finite set of places w at which U_w = U ∩ G(K_w) is not a hyperspecial maximal compact subgroup; at w ∉ S the group G is unramified over K_w.
Corrections PAPER-CIUBOTARU-HARRIS-26/E1 (the conjecture is 9.5, (9.3) a display), E15 (m(π) > 0), E16 (Φ_disc(U) and ι_ℓ in 9.5(2)).
proofSteps: The hypotheses hold for the cuspidal spectrum (RA.2/rational-satake-parameters).

Under (9.1), base change to ℂ gives the finite-dimensional unitary discrete-spectrum module. Its Hecke action is semisimple over ℂ and hence after algebraic scalar extension as used by RA.7/conditional-discrete-rationality. No semisimplicity over an arbitrary characteristic-zero coefficient ring E is asserted.
acceptance: For the cuspidal subspace the hypotheses are theorems of Lafforgue and BHKT.
For PGL₂ the residual characters have the form χ∘det with χ²=1, so that the character descends from GL₂ to PGL₂; their parameters are explicit.

nodes.title: Rationality of the discrete spectrum under the finiteness hypothesis
nodes.statement: Assume Conjecture 9.1 for (G,U). Then the eigenvalues of H^S(G,U) on A_disc(G,U,C) are algebraic, and A_disc(G,U,Q̄)=⊕_{π:π^U≠0}m_U(π)π^U. Each irreducible π occurring at this level has a number-field model. To deduce the assertion for every discrete automorphic π, impose Conjecture 9.1 at all sufficiently small levels.

The assertion about a representation π at fixed level U concerns π with π^U≠0. To assert the result for every discrete automorphic π, assume Conjecture 9.1 at every sufficiently small level.
proofSteps: A_disc(G, U, Q) is a finite-dimensional Q-space stable under the Hecke algebra with integral structure; its eigenvalues are algebraic and the action is semisimple over a large number field, as in Lemma 3.2.

For π^U≠0 use the full level-U Hecke algebra, rather than good-place eigenvalues alone. Its image on the finite-dimensional rational space A_disc(G,U,Q) is a finite-dimensional Q-algebra. Its simple modules have models over finite extensions of Q; the simple Hecke-module/smooth-representation correspondence recovers π from π^U. This also accounts for a finite Schur-index extension. The all-representations assertion uses sufficiently small levels.
acceptance: For the cuspidal spectrum this is RA.2/rational-satake-parameters without hypothesis.

nodes.title: Xue: parametrization of finite-codimension Hecke quotients
nodes.statement: Let G be split reductive over K, N a level, Ξ a cocompact central lattice, u ∉ N a place and 𝔍 an ideal of finite codimension in the spherical Hecke algebra H_{G,u}. Then C_c(Bun_{G,N}(F_q)/Ξ, Q̄_ℓ) is of finite type over H_{G,u} (Proposition 1), so the quotient Q = C_c/𝔍·C_c is finite-dimensional, and Q decomposes canonically as ⊕_σ H_σ over continuous semisimple σ : Weil(K̄/K) → Ĝ(Q̄_ℓ) unramified outside N, H_σ being the generalized eigenspace for the character f((σ(γ_i))) of the excursion algebra; H_σ lies in the generalized eigenspace of T(h_{V,v}) with eigenvalue χ_V(σ(Frob_v)) for v ∉ N. The decomposition is compatible with constant-term morphisms. A discrete automorphic π with a number-field model occurring in such a quotient has a compatible global parameter (RA.7/compatible-global-parameter). For a constituent π the full compact-support comparison of Li-Huerta Theorem 6.13 also identifies σ|_{W_{K_v}}^{ss}=L_{K_v}(π_v) at ramified places, whenever π lies in the chosen σ generalized eigenspace. No algebraicity of eigenvalues for arbitrary coefficient-field ideals 𝔍 is asserted.
hypotheses: K = k₁(X) is the function field of a smooth projective geometrically connected curve X over a finite field k₁ of characteristic p and cardinality q₁; |X| is its set of closed points (places); q_w = |k(w)| for a place w; ℓ ≠ p is a prime.
G split; Hecke operators on Q need not be diagonalizable (Xue Remark 3.6.8).
proofSteps: Finiteness of compactly supported shtuka cohomology over H_{G,u} (Xue Theorem 2; GS.3/single-place-hecke-module-finiteness) gives the Weil^I action via Drinfeld's lemma for finite-type H_{G,u}-modules (GS.4/full-cohomology-weil-descent).

Excursion operators on C_c (GS.5/excursions-on-full-compact-cohomology) descend to Q and generate a finite-dimensional commutative algebra B_𝔍; continuity in (γ_i) (Lemma 3.6.6) and Lafforgue's §11 argument (GS.5/reconstruction-of-a-langlands-parameter) give Theorem 3.6.7.

Satake compatibility is Xue Theorem 3.6.7. For a constituent π with a number-field model, its spherical Hecke character is algebraic, and the normalized Satake isomorphism identifies an algebraic semisimple class with σ(Frob_v). The rational structure on C_c alone does not make an arbitrary Q̄_ℓ-ideal 𝔍 algebraic.

Ciubotaru–Harris (§9.2) speak of ideals of finite codimension in H^S(G, U); such an ideal contains a finite-codimension ideal 𝔍 of a single H_{G,u}, so their quotients are quotients of Xue's Q and inherit the decomposition.

Li-Huerta Theorem 6.13, with Theorem 6.10/§6.11, compares the local excursion algebra via the Bernstein centre with global excursions on the full C_c space. The commuting identity descends to 𝔍-quotients and their generalized eigenspaces. Evaluating its character on a π^U constituent gives the local semisimple parameter, including at ramified v. This uses the full C_c theorem rather than only the cuspidal Theorem A.
acceptance: For 𝔍 the kernel of a character of H_{G,u}, Q is the largest quotient on which H_{G,u} acts by that character (Xue Remark 3.6.3).
On the cuspidal part the decomposition is Lafforgue's.

For the abstract Hecke algebra Q̄_ℓ[T], the codimension-one ideal (T−a) can have a transcendental a over Q. Finite codimension alone is not an algebraicity argument; the positive constituent statement uses the given number-field model.

sources.locator: Introduction, Proposition 1 and Theorem 2, pp. 2–3; §3.6, Definition 3.6.5, Lemma 3.6.6 and Theorem 3.6.7 with Remarks 3.6.3 and 3.6.8, pp. 30–31; §4.2, pp. 40–41
sources.match: Proves finiteness of compactly supported shtuka cohomology over a local Hecke algebra, extends excursion operators to compactly supported automorphic forms and decomposes every finite-codimension Hecke quotient by semisimple Weil-group parameters compatibly with Satake and constant terms.
Cites Xue for the extension of Lafforgue's parametrization to finite-codimension quotients, covering some non-cuspidal discrete representations.

Constructs global excursions on all compactly supported automorphic forms and compares the restricted local excursions with the local Bernstein centre. The identity descends to Hecke quotients and their σ generalized eigenspaces.

nodes.title: Global weight patterns
nodes.statement: Let π have a compatible global parameter σ (RA.7/compatible-global-parameter) such that L(π, τ) has integer weights for every τ (for instance π_u geometric at some place u, by RA.1/geometric-boundary-propagation). The global weight pattern is n(i, π, τ) := rank gr_i^W L(π, τ). For every w ∉ S, the weight pattern of the Satake class s_w(π) (LieHighestWeightPartII N5/weight-pattern, with q = q_w) equals n(·, π, τ) for every τ.
hypotheses: K = k₁(X) is the function field of a smooth projective geometrically connected curve X over a finite field k₁ of characteristic p and cardinality q₁; |X| is its set of closed points (places); q_w = |k(w)| for a place w; ℓ ≠ p is a prime.

Whenever geometricity or an Aubert anchor at u is used, require σ|_{W_{K_u}}^{ss}=L_{K_u}(π_u). This follows for cuspidal parameters by RA.3/local-parametrization and for a chosen Xue quotient eigenspace by RA.7/xue-hecke-quotient-parametrization with Li-Huerta Theorem 6.13. nodes.title: Propagation of complementary series
nodes.statement: Let G be split semisimple over K, π ⊂ A_disc(G, Q̄) with m_U(π) ≠ 0 having a compatible global parameter (RA.7/compatible-global-parameter: π cuspidal, or occurring in a finite-codimension Hecke quotient, or under the hypotheses of RA.7/discrete-spectrum-parametrization). Assume a place u with π_u geometric (RA.3/geometric-representation) and a place v ∉ S with π_v ⊗_ι ℂ in the complementary series CS(G(K_v), O^∨) of a nilpotent orbit O^∨. Then: (a) for every w ∉ S, s_w(π) is geometric with the same weight pattern as s_v(π), so ℜ(s_w) and ℜ(s_v) are Weyl-conjugate; (b) if G is adjoint and s_v and s_w have central compact parts, π_w ⊗_ι ℂ lies in CS(G(K_w), O^∨); (c) if G is adjoint and s_v has central compact part, ℜ(s_v) is the central point ½h^∨ of O^∨ or one of the extraneous points of SRU.7 (restricted lists), and every split w ∉ S has the same real part.

Scope corrections: the parametrization hypothesis is Conjectures 9.1 and 9.5 (PAPER-CIUBOTARU-HARRIS-26/E1); the extraneous lists are those of the real or central-compact sector (E18); the step from equal real parts to membership in the same complementary series needs the compact parts to be central (gap G4).

Whenever geometricity or an Aubert anchor at u is used, require σ|_{W_{K_u}}^{ss}=L_{K_u}(π_u). This follows for cuspidal parameters by RA.3/local-parametrization and for a chosen Xue quotient eigenspace by RA.7/xue-hecke-quotient-parametrization with Li-Huerta Theorem 6.13. For a bare hypothetical parameter known only by good-place Satake compatibility, it is an additional hypothesis.
proofSteps: RA.1/geometric-boundary-propagation at u gives integer weights for every L(π, τ); RA.8/global-weight-pattern makes the weight pattern of s_w independent of w ∉ S.
LieHighestWeightPartII N5/real-part-recognition (Ciubotaru–Harris Proposition 10.2): the weight pattern determines the real part up to conjugacy; this gives (a).

For (b), equality of normalized real parts gives the same root subsets ⟨α,ν⟩=0 and ⟨α,ν⟩=1. With central compact parts these identify the centralizer root algebra and the q_w-eigenspace of Ad(s_w), and similarly at v. Their nilpotent strata match under the root-datum identification; the numerical operators Ad(s_w) and Ad(s_v) need not be equal because q_w can differ from q_v. Unitarity then places π_w in the same complementary-series stratum.

For (c) apply the restricted real/central-compact classifications of SRU.7 componentwise to the simple factors of the split adjoint group. No claim of these classifications for arbitrary compact parts or arbitrary non-adjoint groups is made.
acceptance: For O^∨ = 0 this is the generic statement: the real part is 0 at v and at every w.
Sp(6) dual, O^∨ = (2,2,2): the possible real parts are ½h^∨ = (½, ½, ½) and the extraneous (0, ½, 1) (Remark 8.6).

nodes.title: Property A for symmetric weight arrays
nodes.statement: Let a : ℤ × ℤ → ℕ have finite support and satisfy a(i, i + j) = a(i, i − j) for all i, j; let r(i) = Σ_k a(i, k) and c(i) = Σ_k a(k, i). Then either a is diagonal and r = c, or at the largest index i₀ with r(i₀) ≠ c(i₀) one has c(i₀) > r(i₀).
hypotheses: a has finite support; no other hypothesis.
proofSteps: Downward induction from an index above the support. Suppose r(i) = c(i) for all i > i₁ and that a(i, k) = a(k, i) = 0 for i > i₁, k ≠ i.
Row i₁ is diagonal: a(i₁, k) = 0 for k > i₁ since column k > i₁ is diagonal, and for k < i₁ by symmetry with 2i₁ − k > i₁. Hence r(i₁) = a(i₁, i₁) ≤ c(i₁).
If r(i₁) = c(i₁) then column i₁ is diagonal too and the induction continues; otherwise c(i₁) > r(i₁) at the first (largest) index of difference.
acceptance: The array of Remark 10.8 (a(0, ±1) = 1) has largest difference index 1 with c(1) = 1 > r(1) = 0.
A diagonal array has r = c.

nodes.statement: For each extraneous real part x of SRU.7 (real or central-compact sector) for the orbit O^∨ there is a representation τ of Ĝ and an index i₀ such that n_x(i) = n_{h/2}(i) for i > i₀ and n_x(i₀) > n_{h/2}(i₀), where n_y(i) is the number of weights μ of τ (with multiplicity) with 2⟨μ, y⟩ = i and h/2 is the central point: (1) Ĝ = Sp(2n), τ standard, i₀ the largest even j with r_j ≥ 3 and ε_j = 1, n_x(i₀) = n_{h/2}(i₀) + 1; (2) Ĝ = Spin(n), τ standard, i₀ the largest odd i with r_i ≥ 3 and ε_i = 1, n_x(i₀) = n_{h/2}(i₀) + 1; (3) F₄, τ adjoint: B₃ (x = ω₁ + ½ω₃ + ½ω₄): equal above 8, n_x(8) = 2 > 1; Ã₁ + A₁ (x = ½ω₁ + ½ω₄): n_x(4) = 1 > 0; (4) E₇, τ adjoint, D₅(a₁) + A₁: equal above 9, n_x(9) = 1 > 0; (5) E₈, τ adjoint: D₆, n_x(16) = 2 > 1 with equality above; A₆, n_x(13) = 1 > 0; A₄ + A₂, n_x(9) = 1 > 0; A₂ + 2A₁, n_x(5) = 1 > 0.
hypotheses: Coordinates of Ciubotaru–Harris (6.21), (6.23)–(6.26); corrections PAPER-CIUBOTARU-HARRIS-26/E3 (subscripts) and E5 (the B₃ point).
proofSteps: n_{h/2}(i) is the multiplicity of the eigenvalue i of h on τ, read from the appendix tables for the adjoint representation (LieHighestWeightPartII N3/appendix-table-interface) or from sl₂-theory for the standard representations.
n_x is computed by enumerating the weights of τ in the stated coordinates.

Recomputed for this plan by root enumeration: F₄ B₃ gives n_x(10, 9, 8) = (1, 0, 2) against (1, 0, 1); the printed B₃ point would have top weight 16 (E5); Ã₁ + A₁ gives top weight 4; E₇ gives n_x(10, 9) = (1, 1); E₈ D₆ gives n_x(18, 17, 16) = (1, 0, 2) against (1, 0, 1), A₆, A₄ + A₂, A₂ + 2A₁ give top weights 13, 9, 5 against table maxima 12, 8, 4; Sp(6), (2,2,2): x = (0, ½, 1) gives n_x(2) = 1 against 0.

nodes.title: Elimination of extraneous points
nodes.statement: Under the hypotheses of RA.8/complementary-series-propagation with G adjoint split and s_v of central compact part, assume moreover that u ∈ S and π_u ≅ AZ(σ_u) for an irreducible discrete series σ_u whose pure Weil–Deligne parameter (RA.4/weil-deligne-purity-of-discrete-series) has monodromy in O^∨. Then for every split w ∉ S the real part of the Satake parameter of π_w is the central point ½h^∨ of O^∨; no unramified component is extraneous. Moreover all monodromy operators N_i on (gr_i^W L(π, τ))_u vanish.
hypotheses: K = k₁(X) is the function field of a smooth projective geometrically connected curve X over a finite field k₁ of characteristic p and cardinality q₁; |X| is its set of closed points (places); q_w = |k(w)| for a place w; ℓ ≠ p is a prime.

Q̄ is the algebraic closure of Q inside C, and ι : Q̄ → C, ι_ℓ : Q̄ → Q̄_ℓ are fixed embeddings; a statement 'for every ι' quantifies over all field embeddings Q̄ → C, equivalently over all field isomorphisms Q̄_ℓ ≅ C after extension.
U ⊂ G(A_K) is a compact open subgroup and S = S(U) is the finite set of places w at which U_w = U ∩ G(K_w) is not a hyperspecial maximal compact subgroup; at w ∉ S the group G is unramified over K_w.
Same scope corrections as RA.8/complementary-series-propagation.

Whenever geometricity or an Aubert anchor at u is used, require σ|_{W_{K_u}}^{ss}=L_{K_u}(π_u). This follows for cuspidal parameters by RA.3/local-parametrization and for a chosen Xue quotient eigenspace by RA.7/xue-hecke-quotient-parametrization with Li-Huerta Theorem 6.13. For a bare hypothetical parameter known only by good-place Satake compatibility, it is an additional hypothesis.
proofSteps: L_F(π_u) = L_F(σ_u) (SRU.7/aubert-semisimple-parameter), so n_u is the weight pattern of the Frobenius of the pure parameter of σ_u, whose real part is q_u^{h/2} with h the neutral element of an sl₂-triple through the monodromy (bounded part ϕ₀, RA.4/weil-deligne-purity-of-discrete-series).

By RA.8/complementary-series-propagation (c), ℜ(s_v) is ½h^∨ or extraneous; in the extraneous case RA.8/extraneous-weight-certificates gives τ violating Property A for the array of RA.8/weight-array, contradicting RA.8/property-a.
So n_v = n_u, the pattern of ½h^∨; by RA.8/global-weight-pattern and LieHighestWeightPartII N5/real-part-recognition every split w ∉ S has real part ½h^∨.
With n_u = n_v the array is diagonal (Property A, first alternative), which is the vanishing of every N_i (Remark 10.7).
acceptance: For O^∨ = 0, σ_u supercuspidal and AZ(σ_u) = σ_u: the theorem says the real part is 0 at every split unramified place, recovering the generic statement in that case.

gaps.title: G1. Simple trace formula and Poincaré-series globalization over function fields have no owner
gaps.detail: The Deligne–Kazhdan simple trace formula for general connected reductive groups over a global function field and Gan–Lomelí's Poincaré-series globalization are used as cited theorems; no atlas roadmap plans them (ES7:function-field-automorphic covers only GL_d and division algebras in a selected range). They are requested from a Part II of FunctionFieldArithmetic at FA.6.

gaps.title: G2. Number-field models of arbitrary discrete series
gaps.detail: Ciubotaru–Harris Theorem 4.2 asserts that every complex discrete series of a semisimple group over F = k((t)) has a model over a number field; the sketch derives it from Beuzart-Plessis's lemma, which only gives a cuspidal representation with the same cuspidal support (this packet's source issue E1). The plan proves the Galois conjugation statement for representations that have a number-field model, viewed over Q̄, which covers every local component of a cuspidal representation and every supercuspidal; the model for an arbitrary discrete series (for example by finiteness of discrete series with given cuspidal support and algebraicity of the reducibility points) is not established.

gaps.title: G3. Embedding independence of temperedness without geometricity (E10)
gaps.detail: Ciubotaru–Harris Theorem 4.3 (an ι-tempered component of a cuspidal representation is tempered for every embedding) assumes in step (2) of its sketch that every local monodromy of L(Π, τ) is geometric, which is not known without an anchor (PAPER-CIUBOTARU-HARRIS-26/E10). The plan states the theorem under geometricity of the local parameter and proves the generic theorem for a fixed ι without it.

gaps.title: G4. Non-central compact parts of Satake parameters (E11, E18) and the stratum step of Theorem 1.11
gaps.detail: The local classifications used at v (SRU.5/generic-temperedness-test, SRU.6, SRU.7 extraneous lists) hold for Satake parameters whose compact part is central; for non-central compact parts the G₂ witness (SRU.5/g2-noncentral-witness) shows the generic test fails locally. Theorem 5.4 is therefore planned with the centrality hypothesis at v, and Theorem 1.11 with conclusions (b) and (c) under centrality; an exhaustive classification of geometric complementary-series points with arbitrary compact part (through SRU.7/noncentral-compact-reduction) and a global argument excluding them are missing. No global counterexample is known.

gaps.title: G5. Integrality of weights for direct images from algebraic stacks
gaps.detail: Ciubotaru–Harris Sketch 5.10 requires integer weights for constant-coefficient direct images from finite-type stacks. Sun Theorem 2.11, pp.14–15, gives real ι-mixedness; Remark 2.12 also states preservation of mixedness without a fixed embedding. Neither is silently identified here with preservation of the integer-weight subclass. A closure proof with the exact integer convention, using a smooth presentation, the hypercover spectral sequence and a mixed dualizing complex, is requested at DWP.8. This alternative stack route is not needed by the anchored endpoint.

gaps.title: G6. Elliptic orthogonality of discrete-series characters in positive characteristic
gaps.detail: Beuzart-Plessis's Lemma A.3 uses his elliptic orthogonality relations for discrete-series characters, cited in Gan–Harris–Sawin as a 2022 manuscript; no public version was located for this plan. It is requested at SRU.3 with the pseudo-coefficients it accompanies.

gaps.title: G7. The Annals version of Ciubotaru–Harris is not collated
gaps.detail: All locators are to arXiv v1; the accepted revision (8 October 2025) may already repair E10–E13 and renumber statements. Collate the locators and the corrections when a copy is available.

gaps.title: G8. Reductive central reduction and coefficient normalization
gaps.detail: The all-embeddings arithmetic globalization chain is stated for semisimple G. Its extension to arbitrary reductive centres requires the precise SR.3 central reduction and ES6 parameter transport; fixed-ι boundedness does not prove absolute purity in an arbitrary faithful representation. ES5 must also identify the √q coefficient-automorphism law used by RA.3. These are requested supplier targets, not theorems obtained by the narrower existing nodes.

gaps.title: G9. General adjoint transfer and spherical genericity
gaps.detail: The non-adjoint generic-place reduction must account for the finite-index image on rational points. Nonsplit genericity propagation needs the general unramified quasi-split theorem, not merely SRU.5’s split adjoint criterion. Exact contracts are requested at SR.4; the endpoint remains conditional on those contracts.

gaps.title: G10. From Satake coefficients to constant stack coefficients
gaps.detail: Lafforgue–Zhu’s formula retains Sσ invariants and a frozen auxiliary representation. It does not identify a Satake IC coefficient complex with the constant sheaf. The precise realization bridge requested at DWP.8 is required before deducing the constant-coefficient predicate from that formula.

gaps.title: G11. Weight patterns do not construct a global Arthur homomorphism
gaps.detail: RA.8 determines integer weight multiplicities and normalized real Satake parts. It does not provide a commuting global SL₂ or a globally compatible bounded Weil factor whose products equal the full Satake classes. ArthurPrediction.At includes these additional conjectural requirements; no construction of ψ is claimed.

gaps.title: G12. Semantic identification of exceptional-orbit profiles
gaps.detail: N3 currently supplies E8/F4/G2 profiles with opaque identifiers. The orbit-to-SL₂-triple identifications needed here and the E7 D5(a1)+A1 profile must be supplied before the exceptional cases of RA.8/extraneous-weight-certificates are a closed proof. The Sp6 and F4 explicit numerical tests in Lean do not supply these missing identifications.

sourceIssues.printed: Common-weight purity of an LG-valued parameter is declared independent of the chosen faithful representation for connected reductive G.
sourceIssues.correction: For reductive groups distinguish adjoint analytic essential temperedness from common-weight arithmetic purity in a specified representation. For semisimple groups use weight-0 purity in every algebraic representation. Do not infer arbitrary-faithful common-weight independence.
sourceIssues.reason: For G=G_m and unramified Frobenius q, the identity representation is faithful and pure of weight 2, whereas identity ⊕ trivial is also faithful but has weights 2 and 0. With N=0 no scalar twist makes its two weights equal. Thus the faithful-representation equivalence in these definitions fails for this reductive example; this does not refute the semisimple weight-0 theorem used here.
sourceIssues.known: No correction located in the consulted public material; the packet narrows its purity conventions accordingly.

review.reason: Both representations have trivial kernel, but their N=0 Frobenius weight multisets are {2} and {2,0}. Tensor generation preserves integer geometricity, not a common nonzero weight.

sourceIssues.locator: Published Remark 3.10, p.11, final adjoint-irreducibility assertion; compare HNY §2.4, Theorem 2 and Corollary 2.13, pp.17–18
sourceIssues.printed: The local Kloosterman parameter used at the auxiliary place is said to become irreducible after composition with the adjoint representation.
sourceIssues.correction: Use the absence of a proper Levi, which follows from vanishing adjoint inertia invariants. This does not require the adjoint Weil representation to be irreducible.
sourceIssues.reason: Take G=PGL₂ and odd residue characteristic. HNY Corollary 2.13 puts wild inertia in a nontrivial finite subgroup of a dual maximal torus, with tame inertia acting by the rank-one Coxeter element. The Lie algebra of the centralizer of wild inertia is a one-dimensional toral line. Wild inertia is normal in the full local Weil group, so this line is Weil-stable inside the three-dimensional adjoint representation. Tame inertia acts on it by −1: this is consistent with zero inertia invariants, but disproves irreducibility of the adjoint Weil representation.

review.reason: The wild-inertia centralizer line is a proper local Weil subrepresentation. Vanishing inertia invariants is a different assertion and suffices for the consumer.

restructure.detail: The design brief (#3381) carried nine continuations of GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands in six independent directions: (a) Ramanujan and Arthur weight constraints (Ciubotaru–Harris 2026, route GlobalShtukasPartIIRamanujanArthur, 27 items, plus one Gan–Harris–Sawin item); (b) counting unramified ℓ-adic local systems (Yu 2023, route GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglandsCountingPartII, 77 items); (c) the Langlands correspondence for isocrystals and crystalline companions (Abe 2018, 17 items, and D'Addezio 2023, 2 items, route GlobalShtukasPartIICrystallineCompanions); (d) special cycles on shtuka moduli and the higher Siegel–Weil formula (Yun–Zhang 2017, 33 items; Yun–Zhang 2019, 129 items; Feng–Yun–Zhang 2024, 25 items; route ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil); (e) Tate cohomology of shtukas with mod-p coefficients and cyclic base change (Feng 2024, route ShtukaTateCohomologyAndGlobalBaseChange, 33 items); (f) Ĝ-valued deformation theory and potential automorphy (Böckle–Harris–Khare–Thorne 2019, route GValuedDeformationsAndPotentialAutomorphy, 28 items).
